sentences.zh: 志第二十八食貨上

translations.literal: Treatise Twenty-eight: Economy and Currency, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 28: Economy and Currency (Part One)

sentences.zh: 先王之制，度地以居人，均其沃瘠，差其貢賦，蓋斂之必以道也。

translations.literal: The institutions of the former kings measured land to settle the people, balanced its fertility and barrenness, and graded tribute and levies — for collection must indeed follow the right Way.
translations.idiomatic: In the institutions of the ancient kings, land was surveyed to settle the population, fertility and barrenness were balanced against one another, and tribute and taxes were scaled accordingly — levies had to follow proper principle.

sentences.zh: 量入而為出，節用而愛人，度財省費，蓋用之必有度也，是故既庶且富，而教化行焉。

translations.literal: They measured income to set expenditure, economized in use while cherishing the people, and gauged wealth while sparing expense — for spending must indeed have limits; therefore, when the people were numerous and wealthy, transforming instruction was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue set the bounds of expenditure, frugality was practiced and the people cared for, and costs were weighed and expenses curbed — public spending had to stay within limits; only then could a populous, prosperous realm sustain civilizing order.

sentences.zh: 周有井田之制，秦有阡陌之法，二世發閭左而海內崩離，漢武稅舟車而國用以竭。

translations.literal: Zhou had the well-field system; Qin had the field-path law. The Second Emperor drafted those from the wards' left and the realm within the seas split apart; Emperor Wu taxed boats and carts and state funds were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou instituted the well-field system and Qin the open-field law; when the Second Emperor conscripted commoners wholesale, the empire fell apart, and when Emperor Wu taxed boats and carriages, the treasury was drained dry.

sentences.zh: 自古有國有家，興亡盛衰，未嘗不由此也。

translations.literal: From antiquity, those who possessed states and families — in rise, fall, flourishing, and decay — have never failed to proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity onward, the rise and fall of dynasties has always hinged on such fiscal choices.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝因周氏平齊之後，府庫充實，庶事節儉，未嘗虛費。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui, relying on the Zhou house's pacification of Qi, found the treasuries full and all affairs economical; he never spent wastefully.
translations.idiomatic: After the Northern Zhou pacified Qi, Emperor Wen of Sui inherited full treasuries; he kept ordinary affairs frugal and never squandered public funds.

sentences.zh: 開皇之初，議者以比漢代文、景，有粟陳貫朽之積。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, discussants compared him to Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing of Han; there was grain piled so long that the cords rotted.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaihuang era, commentators likened his reign to those of Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing of Han, when grain stores grew so vast that the ropes binding the sacks rotted away.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，大縱奢靡，加以東西行幸，輿駕不息，征討四夷，兵車屢動。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, he greatly indulged extravagance; moreover he traveled east and west, his carriage never resting, campaigning against the four barbarians, with troops and chariots repeatedly mobilized.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he gave free rein to extravagance, touring east and west without pause, campaigning against the frontier peoples, and mobilizing armies again and again.

sentences.zh: 西失律于沙徼，東喪師於遼、碣，數年之間，公私罄竭，財力既殫，國遂亡矣。

translations.literal: In the west he lost discipline at the desert frontier; in the east he lost armies at Liao and Jie. Within a few years, public and private were exhausted; financial strength was spent, and the state then perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the west his armies broke down on the desert frontier; in the east he lost forces in Liaodong and the Jie region. Within a few years both public and private coffers were empty, the state's resources were spent, and the dynasty collapsed.

sentences.zh: 高祖發跡太原，因晉陽宮留守庫物，以供軍用。

translations.literal: Gaozu rose from Taiyuan and relied on the stored goods of the Jinyang Palace garrison to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu launched his uprising from Taiyuan and drew on the stores of the Jinyang Palace garrison to supply his troops.

sentences.zh: 既平京城，先封府庫，賞賜給用，皆有節制，征斂賦役，務在寬簡。

translations.literal: After pacifying the capital region, he first sealed the treasuries; rewards and grants all had limits, and levies and corvée labor aimed at leniency and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Once the capital was secured, he sealed the treasuries first; rewards and disbursements were kept within bounds, and tax levies and corvée were kept light and simple.

sentences.zh: 未及逾年，遂成帝業。

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed, he thus completed the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a year he had secured the throne.

sentences.zh: 其後掌財賦者，世有人焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter, those in charge of wealth and levies — in every generation there were such men.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, each generation produced men charged with managing the state's finances.

sentences.zh: 開元已前，事歸尚書省，開元已後，權移他官。

translations.literal: Before the Kaiyuan era, affairs belonged to the Department of State Affairs; after Kaiyuan, authority shifted to other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Kaiyuan era fiscal affairs belonged to the Department of State Affairs; after Kaiyuan, authority shifted to other offices.

sentences.zh: 由是有轉運使、租庸使、鹽鐵使、度支鹽鐵轉運使、常平鑄錢鹽鐵使、租庸青苗使、水陸運鹽鐵租庸使、兩稅使，隨事立名，沿革不一。

translations.literal: Hence there arose transport commissioners, zu-yong commissioners, salt-and-iron commissioners, revenue salt-and-iron transport commissioners, ever-normal coin-casting salt-and-iron commissioners, zu-yong green-sprout commissioners, water-and-land transport salt-and-iron zu-yong commissioners, and dual-tax commissioners — titles established as affairs arose, with changes not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Hence came transport commissioners, zu-yong commissioners, salt-and-iron commissioners, and many combined titles — the dual-tax commissioner among them — each created for the task at hand, with names and duties shifting over time.

sentences.zh: 設官分職，選賢任能，得其人則有益於國家，非其才則貽患于黎庶，此又不可不知也。

translations.literal: Establishing offices and dividing duties, selecting the worthy and employing the capable — if one obtains the right man, the state benefits; if not his talent, harm reaches the common people. This too must not go unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were established and duties divided, the worthy selected and the capable employed — the right appointee benefited the state, the wrong one brought harm to the people. This too must be understood.

sentences.zh: 如裴耀卿、劉晏、李巽數君子，便時利物，富國安民，足為世法者也。

translations.literal: Such gentlemen as Pei Yaoxing, Liu Yan, and Li Xun — adapting to the times and benefiting things, enriching the state and securing the people — are sufficient to serve as models for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Pei Yaoxing, Liu Yan, and Li Xun adapted policy to the times, enriched the state, and secured the people — they are fit to serve as models for later ages.

sentences.zh: 開元中，有御史宇文融獻策，括籍外剩田：色役偽濫，及逃戶許歸首，免五年征賦。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Censor Yuwen Rong presented a plan to register surplus fields outside the rolls: fraudulent color-service corvée, and allowing fugitive households to surrender with five years of levies waived.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era, Censor Yuwen Rong proposed registering unreported surplus land, cracking down on fraudulent corvée exemptions, and allowing fugitive households to register voluntarily with five years of taxes forgiven.

sentences.zh: 每丁量稅一千五百錢，置攝御史，分路檢括隱審。

translations.literal: Each adult male was assessed tax of 1,500 cash; acting censors were appointed to inspect and verify concealment by route.
translations.idiomatic: Each adult male was assessed 1,500 cash in tax, and acting censors were dispatched along the routes to investigate concealed households.

sentences.zh: 得戶八十余萬，田亦稱是，得錢數百萬貫，玄宗以為能，數年間拔為御史中丞、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: They obtained more than 800,000 households, and fields in proportion; they obtained several million strings of cash. Xuanzong regarded him as capable, and within a few years promoted him to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: More than 800,000 households were registered, with a proportional amount of land, yielding several million strings of cash. Xuanzong judged him capable and within a few years promoted him to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 融又畫策開河北王莽河，溉田數千頃，以營稻田，事未果而融敗。

translations.literal: Rong also devised a plan to open the Wang Mang River in Hebei, irrigating several thousand qing of fields to establish rice paddies; the affair did not succeed before Rong fell.
translations.idiomatic: Rong also proposed opening the Wang Mang River in Hebei to irrigate thousands of qing for rice paddies, but the project never succeeded before his downfall.

sentences.zh: 時又楊崇禮為太府卿，清嚴善勾剝，分寸錙銖，躬親不厭。

translations.literal: At the same time Yang Chongli served as Director of the Palace Storehouse, stern and skilled at exacting collection, down to fen and zhu, personally attending without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Yang Chongli served as Director of the Palace Storehouse; austere and relentless in collection, he personally scrutinized every fraction down to the smallest weight without tiring.

sentences.zh: 轉輸納欠，折估漬損，必令征送。

translations.literal: For transport deliveries in arrears, or valuation discounts for spoilage, he always compelled collection and delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Shortfalls in transport deliveries, discounted valuations for spoilage — he always compelled full payment.

sentences.zh: 天下州縣征財帛，四時不止。

translations.literal: Throughout the empire's prefectures and counties, collection of wealth and silks never ceased through the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties across the empire collected wealth and silks without pause through all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 及老病致仕，以其子慎矜為御史，專知太府出納。

translations.literal: When old age and illness led him to retire, his son Shenjin was made censor, exclusively in charge of Palace Storehouse receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: When age and illness forced his retirement, his son Shenjin was appointed censor with sole charge of Palace Storehouse receipts and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 其弟慎名又專知京倉，皆以苛刻害人，承主恩而征責。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shenming in turn was exclusively in charge of the capital granaries; both were harsh and harmed people, relying on imperial favor to levy and exact.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shenming took charge of the capital granaries; both brothers oppressed the people with harsh exactions, secure in the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 又有韋堅，規宇文融、楊慎矜之跡，乃請于江淮轉運租米，取州縣義倉粟，轉市輕貨，差富戶押船，若遲留損壞，皆征船戶。

translations.literal: There was also Wei Jian, who patterned himself on Yuwen Rong and Yang Shenjin; he requested to transport rent grain on the Jiang-Huai routes, take righteous-granary grain from prefectures and counties, convert it to light goods, assign wealthy households to guarantee boats — if there was delay, retention, or damage, all were levied on the boat households.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian followed in the footsteps of Yuwen Rong and Yang Shenjin; he proposed shipping rent grain from the Jiang-Huai region, drawing on county righteous-granary stores to trade for light goods, and assigning wealthy households to guarantee the boats — any delay, detention, or damage was charged to the boat owners.

sentences.zh: 關中漕渠，鑿廣運潭以挽山東之粟，歲四百萬石，帝以為能，又至貴盛。

translations.literal: For the Guanzhong transport canals, he excavated the Guangyun Pool to draw grain from east of the mountains — four million shi per year. The emperor regarded him as capable, and he again reached exalted eminence.
translations.idiomatic: For the Guanzhong transport canals he excavated the Guangyun Pool to draw grain from east of the mountains — four million shi per year. The emperor judged him capable and he rose to the highest favor.

sentences.zh: 又王鉷進計，奮身自為戶口色役使，征剝財貨，每歲進錢百億，寶貨稱是。

translations.literal: Also Wang Hong advanced plans, throwing himself into serving as household-and-color-service commissioner, exacting wealth and goods; each year he presented ten billion in cash, with treasures and goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong advanced his own schemes, taking the post of household-and-corvée commissioner himself and exacting wealth; each year he presented ten billion in cash, with treasures and goods to match.

sentences.zh: 雲非正額租庸，便入百寶大盈庫，以供人主宴私賞賜之用。

translations.literal: They said it was not regular-quota zu and yong; it then entered the Hundred Treasures Great Surplus Storehouse to supply the ruler's banquets, private pleasures, and bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Funds outside the regular zu-yong quotas went straight into the Hundred Treasures Great Surplus Storehouse to supply the emperor's banquets, private pleasures, and gifts.

sentences.zh: 玄宗日益眷之，數年間亦為御史大夫、京兆尹、帶二十餘使。

translations.literal: Xuanzong daily favored him more; within a few years he also became Censor-in-Chief, Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and held more than twenty commissioner posts concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong favored him ever more; within a few years he was also Censor-in-Chief and Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, holding more than twenty concurrent commissioner posts.

sentences.zh: 又楊國忠藉椒房之勢，承恩幸，帶四十餘使，雲經其聽覽，必數倍弘益，又見寵貴。

translations.literal: Also Yang Guozhong relied on empress-clan power, received favor, held more than forty commissioner posts, and claimed that whatever passed his review must be multiplied several fold in benefit; he too was seen in favored eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong relied on his ties to the imperial consort clan, enjoyed the emperor's favor, held more than forty commissioner posts, and boasted that whatever passed his review yielded several times the usual revenue — he too rose to exalted favor.

sentences.zh: 太平既久，天下至安，人不願亂。

translations.literal: Peace had long endured; the realm was utterly secure; people did not wish for disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had lasted so long that the realm was utterly secure and no one wished for upheaval.

sentences.zh: 而此數人，設詭計以侵擾之，凡二十五人，同為剝喪，而人無敢言之者。

translations.literal: Yet these several men devised crafty schemes to harass them; altogether twenty-five men together stripped and ruined the people, yet none dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these men devised schemes to harass the people; twenty-five of them together stripped the realm bare, and no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反于范陽，兩京倉庫盈溢而不可名。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang, the storehouses of the two capitals overflowed beyond naming.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang, the storehouses of the two capitals overflowed beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠設計，稱不可耗正庫之物，乃使御史崔眾於河東納錢度僧、尼、道士，旬日間行錢百萬。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong devised a plan, saying the regular treasury's goods could not be depleted; he had Censor Cui Zhong at Hedong accept cash to ordain monks, nuns, and Daoist priests — within ten days a million in cash circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong devised a scheme, claiming the regular treasuries could not be touched, and had Censor Cui Zhong at Hedong accept cash to ordain monks, nuns, and Daoist priests — within ten days a million in cash changed hands.

sentences.zh: 玄宗幸巴蜀，鄭昉使劍南，請於江陵稅鹽麻以資國，官置吏以督之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong traveled to Ba-Shu; Zheng Fang was sent to Jiannan and requested taxing salt and hemp at Jiangling to fund the state, with officials appointed to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong fled to Ba-Shu, Zheng Fang was sent to Jiannan and proposed taxing salt and hemp at Jiangling to fund the state, with officials appointed to enforce collection.

sentences.zh: 肅宗建號于靈武，後用雲間鄭叔清為御史，于江淮間豪族富商率貸及賣官爵，以裨國用。

translations.literal: Suzong established his reign-title at Lingwu; later he employed Zheng Shuqing of Yunjian as censor, and among powerful clans and wealthy merchants between the Jiang and Huai he compelled loans and sold offices and ranks to supplement state use.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong proclaimed his reign at Lingwu; later he appointed Zheng Shuqing of Yunjian as censor to compel loans from wealthy Jiang-Huai clans and sell offices and ranks to supplement state revenue.

sentences.zh: 德宗朝討河朔及李希烈，物力耗竭。

translations.literal: In Dezong's court, campaigns against Hebei and Li Xilie exhausted material resources.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong, campaigns against Hebei and Li Xilie drained the state's material resources.

sentences.zh: 趙贊司國計，纖瑣刻剝，以為國用不足，宜賦取於下，以資軍蓄。

translations.literal: Zhao Zan managed state accounts, minutely exacting and stripping; he held that state funds were insufficient and levies should be taken from below to supply military stores.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zan managed state finances with petty, relentless exactions; he argued that revenue was insufficient and that levies should be drawn from the populace to fund military stores.

sentences.zh: 與諫官陳京等更陳計策，贊請稅京師居人屋宅，據其間架差等計入。

translations.literal: With remonstrance officials such as Chen Jing he repeatedly presented plans; Zan requested taxing the dwellings of capital residents, assessing them by the graded intervals of their structures.
translations.idiomatic: Together with remonstrance officials such as Chen Jing he presented further schemes; Zhao Zan proposed taxing dwellings in the capital according to the size and grade of their structures.

sentences.zh: 陳京又請籍列肆商賈資產，以分數借之。

translations.literal: Chen Jing also requested registering and listing shop merchants' assets to lend against them by graded shares.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing also proposed registering merchants' assets in the market wards and compelling graded loans against them.

sentences.zh: 宰相同為欺罔，遂行其計。

translations.literal: The chief ministers together practiced deception, and thus his plans were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers colluded in the deception and the plans were enacted.

sentences.zh: 中外沸騰，人懷怨望。

translations.literal: Within and without seethed; people harbored resentment and longing for relief.
translations.idiomatic: The court and the country seethed with outrage and popular resentment.

sentences.zh: 時又配王公已下及嘗在方鎮之家出家僮及馬以助征行，公私囂然矣。

translations.literal: At the time they also assigned male servants and horses from princes and dukes downward and from families that had served in frontier commands to aid the campaign — public and private were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: At the time male servants and horses were also requisitioned from princes and dukes downward and from families that had held frontier commands to support the campaigns, and public and private alike were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 後又張滂、裴延齡、王涯等，剝下媚上，此皆足為世戒者也。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Pang, Pei Yanling, Wang Ya, and others stripped those below while flattering those above — all sufficient to serve as warnings for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Pang, Pei Yanling, Wang Ya, and others stripped the people to please their superiors — each a warning for later ages.

sentences.zh: 先是興元克復京師後，府藏盡虛，諸道初有進奉，以資經費，復時有宣索。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Xingyuan recovered the capital, the treasuries were utterly empty; the various circuits at first made presentation offerings to fund expenses, and there were also repeated imperial requisitions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the court recovered the capital from its refuge at Xingyuan, the treasuries were empty; the circuits first began presentation offerings to fund expenses, and the throne also issued repeated requisitions.

sentences.zh: 其後諸賊既平，朝廷無事，常賦之外，進奉不息。

translations.literal: Thereafter, once the various rebels were pacified and the court had no urgent affairs, beyond regular levies the presentation offerings never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were pacified and the court had no pressing crises, presentation offerings beyond regular taxes never ceased.

sentences.zh: 韋皋劍南有日進，李兼江西有月進。

translations.literal: Wei Gao in Jiannan had daily presentations; Li Jian in Jiangxi had monthly presentations.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao in Jiannan sent daily presentations; Li Jian in Jiangxi sent monthly presentations.

sentences.zh: 杜亞揚州、劉贊宣州、王緯李錡浙西，皆競為進奉，以固恩澤。

translations.literal: Du Ya at Yangzhou, Liu Zan at Xuanzhou, Wang Wei and Li Qi in western Zhe — all competed in presentation offerings to secure imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya at Yangzhou, Liu Zan at Xuanzhou, and Wang Wei and Li Qi in western Zhe all competed in presentation offerings to secure imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 貢入之奏，皆白臣於正稅外方圓，亦曰「羨餘」。

translations.literal: Memorials on tribute submitted all stated plainly that beyond regular taxes there was surplus, also called "surplus remainder."
translations.idiomatic: Memorials on tribute submitted all reported surplus beyond regular taxes, also called "surplus remainder."

sentences.zh: 節度使或托言密旨，乘此盜貿官物。

translations.literal: Military commissioners sometimes claimed secret edicts and used this to trade illicitly in official goods.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioners sometimes claimed secret edicts and used the pretense to trade illicitly in official goods.

sentences.zh: 諸道有謫罰官吏入其財者，刻祿廩，通津達道者稅之，蒔蔬藝果者稅之，死亡者稅之。

translations.literal: In the various circuits, when punished and demoted officials' wealth was taken in, they carved away salaries and granaries; they taxed those on thoroughfares and major routes; they taxed those planting vegetables and cultivating fruit; they taxed the dead.
translations.idiomatic: In the circuits, wealth seized from punished officials was absorbed into local coffers; salaries and granary allotments were cut; travelers on major routes were taxed, gardeners and orchardists were taxed, even the dead were taxed.

sentences.zh: 節度觀察交代，或先期稅入以為進奉。

translations.literal: When military commissioners and surveillance commissioners transferred office, some levied taxes in advance for presentation offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When military and surveillance commissioners transferred office, some collected taxes in advance for presentation offerings.

sentences.zh: 然十獻其二三耳，其餘沒入，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Yet of ten parts only two or three were presented; the rest was absorbed, beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet only two or three parts in ten reached the throne; the rest was absorbed locally, beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 此節度使進奉也。

translations.literal: This was presentation offerings by military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Such was presentation offering by military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 其後裴肅為常州刺史，乃鬻貨薪炭案牘，百賈之上，皆規利焉。

translations.literal: Later Pei Su served as prefect of Changzhou; he then sold goods — fuel, charcoal, and documents — and above a hundred trades all sought profit.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Pei Su served as prefect of Changzhou, he sold fuel, charcoal, and office supplies, and profited from more than a hundred kinds of trade.

sentences.zh: 歲餘又進奉。

translations.literal: Within a year he again made presentation offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he again sent presentation offerings.

sentences.zh: 無幾，遷浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 天下刺史進奉，自肅始也。

translations.literal: Presentation offerings by prefects throughout the realm began with Su.
translations.idiomatic: Presentation offerings by prefects throughout the empire began with Pei Su.

sentences.zh: 劉贊死于宣州，嚴綬為判官，傾軍府資用進奉。

translations.literal: Liu Zan died at Xuanzhou; Yan Shou served as aide and poured out the military prefecture's resources for presentation offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zan died at Xuanzhou, Yan Shou as his aide drained the military prefecture's resources for presentation offerings.

sentences.zh: 無幾，拜刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 天下判官進奉，自綬始也。

translations.literal: Presentation offerings by aides throughout the realm began with Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Presentation offerings by prefectural aides throughout the empire began with Yan Shou.

sentences.zh: 習以為常，流宕忘返。

translations.literal: It became habit and custom, drifting on without return.
translations.idiomatic: The practice became routine, and the court drifted on without turning back.

sentences.zh: 大抵有唐之禦天下也，有兩稅焉，有鹽鐵焉，有漕運焉，有倉廩焉，有雜稅焉。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, in Tang's governing of the realm there were the dual tax, salt and iron, transport, granaries, and miscellaneous levies.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, Tang governance of the realm rested on the dual tax, salt and iron monopolies, grain transport, state granaries, and miscellaneous levies.

sentences.zh: 今考其本末，敘其否臧，以為《食貨志》云。

translations.literal: Now I examine their origins and ends, narrate their failures and successes, to compose the Treatise on Economy and Currency.
translations.idiomatic: Here I examine their origins and outcomes, recount their failures and successes, and compose this Treatise on Economy and Currency.

sentences.zh: 武德七年，始定律令。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wude, statutes and ordinances were first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wude (624), the statutes and ordinances were first promulgated.

sentences.zh: 以度田之制：五尺為步，步二百四十為畝，畝百為頃。

translations.literal: As to the land-measurement system: five chi made one bu, 240 bu made one mu, and 100 mu made one qing.
translations.idiomatic: The land-measurement system fixed five chi to the bu, 240 bu to the mu, and 100 mu to the qing.

sentences.zh: 丁男、中男給一頃，篤疾、廢疾給四十畝，寡妻妾三十畝。

translations.literal: Adult males and medium males were granted one qing; those with severe or crippling illness forty mu; widows and concubines thirty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Adult and medium males received one qing; those with severe or crippling illness received forty mu; widows and concubines received thirty mu.

sentences.zh: 若為戶者加二十畝。

translations.literal: If one headed a household, twenty mu were added.
translations.idiomatic: Household heads received an additional twenty mu.

sentences.zh: 所授之田，十分之二為世業，八為口分。

translations.literal: Of the land granted, two-tenths were hereditary estate and eight-tenths were per-capita allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Of the land granted, two-tenths were hereditary estate and eight-tenths were per-capita allotment subject to recall.

sentences.zh: 世業之田，身死則承戶者便授之；

translations.literal: Hereditary-estate land: when the holder died, the heir who succeeded the household was immediately granted it;
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary-estate land passed on death to the heir who succeeded the household;

sentences.zh: 口分，則收入官，更以給人。

translations.literal: per-capita allotment was received back by the state and granted again to others.
translations.idiomatic: per-capita allotment reverted to the state and was reallocated to others.

sentences.zh: 賦役之法：每丁歲入租粟二石。

translations.literal: The levy-and-corvée law: each adult male annually paid in two shi of grain as land tax.
translations.idiomatic: Under the levy-and-corvée system, each adult male paid two shi of grain annually as land tax.

sentences.zh: 調則隨鄉土所產，綾、絹、絁各二丈，布加五分之一。

translations.literal: The diao levy followed local products: two zhang each of damask, silk, and coarse silk; for cloth, one-fifth was added.
translations.idiomatic: The diao levy followed local products: two zhang each of damask, silk, and coarse silk; cloth payers owed an additional one-fifth.

sentences.zh: 輸綾、絹、絁者，兼調綿三兩；

translations.literal: Those submitting damask, silk, or coarse silk also paid three liang of cotton in the diao levy;
translations.idiomatic: Those paying damask, silk, or coarse silk also owed three liang of cotton in the diao levy;

sentences.zh: 輸布者，麻三斤。

translations.literal: those submitting cloth paid three jin of hemp.
translations.idiomatic: those paying in cloth owed three jin of hemp.

sentences.zh: 凡丁，歲役二旬。

translations.literal: All adult males served corvée twenty days per year.
translations.idiomatic: All adult males owed twenty days of corvée labor per year.

sentences.zh: 若不役，則收其傭，每日三尺。

translations.literal: If they did not serve, their corvée payment was collected at three chi per day.
translations.idiomatic: If they did not serve in person, a corvée payment of three chi of cloth per day was collected instead.

sentences.zh: 有事而加役者，旬有五日免其調，三旬則租調俱免。

translations.literal: When special affairs added corvée, fifteen days exempted the diao levy; thirty days exempted both land tax and diao.
translations.idiomatic: When extra corvée was imposed for special projects, fifteen days of service exempted the diao levy, and thirty days exempted both land tax and diao.

sentences.zh: 通正役，並不過五十日。

translations.literal: Regular corvée in total did not exceed fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: Regular corvée in total could not exceed fifty days.

sentences.zh: 若嶺南諸州則稅米，上戶一石二斗，次戶八斗，下戶六斗。

translations.literal: In the southern Ling prefectures they taxed rice: upper households one shi two dou, middle households eight dou, lower households six dou.
translations.idiomatic: In the southern Ling prefectures rice was taxed instead: upper households one shi two dou, middle households eight dou, lower households six dou.

sentences.zh: 若夷獠之戶，皆從半輸。

translations.literal: Barbarian and Liao households all paid at half rate.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian and indigenous households all paid at half the standard rate.

sentences.zh: 蕃胡內附者，上戶丁稅錢十文，次戶五文，下戶免之。

translations.literal: For attached Fan and Hu, upper households paid ten wen per adult male, middle households five wen, lower households were exempt.
translations.idiomatic: For attached frontier peoples, upper households paid ten wen per adult male, middle households five wen, and lower households were exempt.

sentences.zh: 附經二年者，上戶丁輸羊二口，次戶一口，下，三戶共一口。

translations.literal: After two years of attachment, upper households paid two sheep per adult male, middle households one, lower households one sheep per three households.
translations.idiomatic: After two years of attachment, upper households owed two sheep per adult male, middle households one, and lower households one sheep per three households.

sentences.zh: 凡水旱蟲霜為災，十分損四已上免租，損六已上免調，損七已上課役俱免。

translations.literal: Whenever flood, drought, insects, or frost caused disaster: loss of four-tenths or more exempted land tax; six-tenths or more exempted diao; seven-tenths or more exempted all levies and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: When flood, drought, insects, or frost caused crop failure, losses of four-tenths or more exempted land tax, six-tenths or more exempted diao, and seven-tenths or more exempted all levies and corvée.

sentences.zh: 凡天下人戶，量其資產，定為九等。

translations.literal: For all households in the realm, their assets were measured and they were fixed in nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: All households in the realm were graded into nine ranks according to assessed assets.

sentences.zh: 每三年，縣司註定，州司覆之。

translations.literal: Every three years the county office registered them and the prefecture office reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years the county office registered the grades and the prefecture office reviewed them.

sentences.zh: 百戶為裏，五里為鄉。

translations.literal: A hundred households made a li; five li made a xiang.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred households formed a li; five li formed a xiang.

sentences.zh: 四家為鄰，五家為保。

translations.literal: Four households made a lin; five households made a bao.
translations.idiomatic: Four households formed a lin; five households formed a bao.

sentences.zh: 在邑居者為坊，在田野者為村。

translations.literal: Those dwelling in towns were in wards; those in the fields were in villages.
translations.idiomatic: Urban residents were organized into wards; rural residents into villages.

sentences.zh: 村坊鄰里，遞相督察。

translations.literal: Villages, wards, lin, and li mutually supervised one another.
translations.idiomatic: Villages, wards, lin, and li mutually supervised one another.

sentences.zh: 士農工商，四人各業。

translations.literal: Scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants — the four groups each had their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants — each group pursued its own occupation.

sentences.zh: 食祿之家，不得與下人爭利。

translations.literal: Families receiving stipends might not compete for profit with commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Officials on stipend might not compete for profit with commoners.

sentences.zh: 工商雜類，不得預于士伍。

translations.literal: Artisans, merchants, and miscellaneous classes might not participate in the scholar ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans, merchants, and miscellaneous classes were barred from the scholar-official ranks.

sentences.zh: 男女始生者為黃，四歲為小，十六為中，二十一為丁，六十為老。

translations.literal: Male and female newborns were "yellow"; at four, "small"; at sixteen, "medium"; at twenty-one, "adult male"; at sixty, "old."
translations.idiomatic: Newborns were classified as "infant"; at four years, "minor"; at sixteen, "medium"; at twenty-one, "adult male"; at sixty, "elder."

sentences.zh: 每歲一造計帳，三年一造戶籍。

translations.literal: Each year an accounting register was compiled; every three years a household register.
translations.idiomatic: An accounting register was compiled annually and a household register every three years.

sentences.zh: 州縣留五比，尚書省留三比。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties retained five copies; the Department of State Affairs retained three.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties retained five copies; the Department of State Affairs retained three.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，韋庶人為皇后，務欲求媚於人，上表請以二十二為丁，五十八為老，制從之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, the Deposed Wei was empress and strove to curry favor; she memorialized requesting that twenty-two be adult male and fifty-eight be old, and the edict followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong (705), Empress Wei sought popular favor and memorialized that adult-male status begin at twenty-two and elder status at fifty-eight; the edict approved her request.

sentences.zh: 及韋氏誅，復舊。

translations.literal: When the Wei clan was executed, the former rules were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei clan was overthrown, the former rules were restored.

sentences.zh: 至天寶三年，又降優制，以十八為中男，二十二為丁。

translations.literal: By the third year of Tianbao, another lenient edict was issued: eighteen was [set as] medium male, twenty-two as adult male.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianbao (744), another lenient edict fixed medium-male status at eighteen and adult-male (ding) status at twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 天下籍始造四本，京師及東京尚書省、戶部各貯一本，以備車駕行幸，省于載運之費焉。

translations.literal: Household registers under Heaven were first made in four copies; the capital and the Eastern Capital each stored one copy in the Department of State Affairs and one in the Board of Revenue, to supply imperial tours and thereby save transport costs.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers were first compiled in four copies nationwide: one each in the capital and Eastern Capital, held by the Department of State Affairs and the Board of Revenue, so that imperial tours could be supplied locally and the cost of transport saved.

sentences.zh: 凡權衡度量之制：度，以北方秬黍中者一黍之廣為分，十分為寸，十寸為尺，十尺為丈。

translations.literal: As to the system of weights, balance, and measures: for length, the width of one grain of medium black millet from the north was taken as one fen; ten fen made one cun, ten cun one chi, ten chi one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The standards for weights, balances, and measures were as follows. For length, one fen was the width of a single grain of medium-sized black millet from the north; ten fen made a cun, ten cun a chi, and ten chi a zhang.

sentences.zh: 量，以秬黍中者容一千二百為龠，二龠為合，十合為升，十升為鬥；

translations.literal: For capacity, one yue held 1,200 grains of medium black millet; two yue made one he, ten he one sheng, ten sheng one dou;
translations.idiomatic: For capacity, the yue held 1,200 grains of medium black millet; two yue made a he, ten he a sheng, and ten sheng a dou;

sentences.zh: 三升為大升，三斗為大鬥，十大鬥為斛。

translations.literal: Three sheng made a large sheng, three dou a large dou, ten large dou one hu.
translations.idiomatic: Three sheng made a large sheng, three dou a large dou, and ten large dou a hu.

sentences.zh: 權衡：以秬黍中者百黍之重為銖，二十四銖為兩，三兩為大兩，十六兩為斤。

translations.literal: For weights and balance: the weight of one hundred grains of medium black millet was one zhu; twenty-four zhu made one liang, three liang a large liang, sixteen liang one jin.
translations.idiomatic: For weights, one zhu was the weight of one hundred grains of medium black millet; twenty-four zhu made a liang, three liang a large liang, and sixteen liang a jin.

sentences.zh: 調鐘律，測晷景，合湯藥及冠冕，制用小升小兩，自餘公私用大升大兩。

translations.literal: For tuning bell pitch-pipes, measuring gnomon shadows, compounding medicines and decoctions, and making caps and crowns, the small sheng and small liang were used by regulation; for all other public and private affairs, the large sheng and large liang were used.
translations.idiomatic: Tuning pitch-pipes, measuring the gnomon shadow, compounding medicines, and making caps and formal headwear required the small sheng and small liang; all other public and private use employed the large sheng and large liang.

sentences.zh: 又山東諸州，以一尺二寸為大尺，人間行用之。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the eastern provinces, one chi two cun was taken as the large chi, used in daily practice among the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern provinces, moreover, the large chi of one chi two cun was the measure used in everyday life.

sentences.zh: 其量制，公私又不用龠，合內之分，則有抄撮之細。

translations.literal: As to the capacity system, public and private use likewise did not employ the yue; within the he, for fractional parts there were the fine units chao and shao.
translations.idiomatic: In practice, neither public nor private use employed the yue; within the he, finer divisions were measured in chao and shao.

sentences.zh: 天寶九載二月，敕：「車軸長七尺二寸，面三斤四兩，鹽鬥，量除陌錢每貫二十文。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year of Tianbao, an edict [stated]: "Cart axles shall be seven chi two cun in length, the wheel iron three jin four liang; the salt dou; for measuring cash deductions from moke money, twenty cash per string of 1,000."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianbao 9 (750), an edict fixed cart axles at seven chi two cun, wheel iron at three jin four liang, specified the salt dou, and set the moke-money deduction at twenty cash per string of 1,000.

sentences.zh: 」先是，開元八年正月，敕：「頃者以庸調無憑，好惡須准，故遣作樣以頒諸州，令其好不得過精，惡不得至濫，任土作貢，防源斯在。

translations.literal: " Earlier, in the first month of the eighth year of Kaiyuan, an edict [stated]: "Recently, because zu-yong and diao had no fixed standard and quality had to be regulated, samples were made and sent to the provinces, requiring that fine goods not exceed the standard and coarse goods not fall below it, allowing local tribute according to local products — therein lay the guard against abuse at the source.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the first month of Kaiyuan 8 (720), an edict had declared: "Because zu-yong and diao lacked a fixed standard and quality had to be regulated, sample pieces were made and sent to the provinces, stipulating that fine goods not exceed the norm and coarse goods not fall to shoddy grade, with tribute following local products — the safeguard against abuse at the source."

sentences.zh: 而諸州送物，作巧生端，苟欲副於斤兩，遂則加其丈尺，至有五丈為疋者，理甚不然。

translations.literal: But the provinces, when submitting goods, contrived tricks; wishing merely to meet the weight in jin and liang, they then increased the length in zhang and chi, until one bolt (pi) reached five zhang — quite unreasonable in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the provinces submitted goods, they contrived evasions: to meet the weight in jin and liang alone, they inflated length in zhang and chi until a single bolt reached five zhang — a practice plainly unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 闊一尺八寸，長四丈，同文共軌，其事久行，立樣之時，亦載此數。

translations.literal: Width one chi eight cun, length four zhang — one standard for all, long in practice; when the sample was established, these numbers were also recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Width of one chi eight cun and length of four zhang had long been the common standard; when the sample was issued, these figures were recorded as well.

sentences.zh: 若求兩而加尺，甚暮四而朝三。

translations.literal: If one seeks to meet the liang by adding chi, it is very much like 'four in the evening, three in the morning.'
translations.idiomatic: To meet the liang by adding chi is very much the trick of 'three in the morning, four in the evening' — a swap in form that changes nothing in substance.

sentences.zh: 宜令所司簡閱，有逾於比年常例，丈尺過多，奏聞。

translations.literal: It is proper to order the responsible offices to review; where goods exceed the usual precedents of recent years and the length in zhang and chi is excessive, report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices should be ordered to review submissions; where goods exceed recent-year precedent and length in zhang and chi is excessive, the matter should be reported to the throne.
Close of edict.

sentences.zh: 二十二年五月，敕：「定戶口之時，百姓非商戶郭外居宅及每丁一牛，不得將入貨財數。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-second year, an edict [stated]: "When household registers are fixed, commoners, except for merchant households' extramural residences and one ox per adult male, may not include goods and property in the count.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kaiyuan 22 (734), an edict declared: "When household registers are compiled, commoners may not enter goods and property in the count, except merchant households' extramural residences and one ox per adult male."

sentences.zh: 其雜匠及幕士並諸色同類，有蕃役合免征行者，一戶之內，四丁已上，任此色役不得過兩人，三丁已上，不得過一人。

translations.literal: As for miscellaneous artisans and tent guards and all similar categories who had frontier service qualifying for corvée exemption: within one household, where there were four adult males or more, no more than two in such categories could serve; where three adult males or more, no more than one.
translations.idiomatic: For miscellaneous artisans, tent guards, and others of the same kind whose frontier service qualified them for corvée exemption: in households of four adult males or more, no more than two such men could hold these posts; in households of three or more, no more than one.

sentences.zh: 」其年七月十八日，敕：「自今已後，京兆府關內諸州，應徵庸調及資課，並限十月三十日畢。

translations.literal: " On the eighteenth day of the seventh month of that year, an edict [stated]: "From now on, for Jingzhao Prefecture and the Guannei provinces, all zu-yong, diao, and supplementary levies due shall be completed by the thirtieth day of the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the seventh month of that year, an edict ordered: "Henceforth, for Jingzhao Prefecture and the Guannei provinces, all zu-yong, diao, and supplementary levies due must be completed by the thirtieth day of the tenth month."

sentences.zh: 」至天寶三載二月二十五日赦文：「每載庸調八月征，以農功未畢，恐難濟辦。

translations.literal: " By the amnesty of the twenty-fifth day of the second month of the third year of Tianbao: "Each year zu-yong and diao are collected in the eighth month; because farm work is not yet finished, completion may be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: By the amnesty of the twenty-fifth day of the second month of Tianbao 3 (744): "Zu-yong and diao are collected each year in the eighth month; because the harvest is not yet complete, timely payment may be difficult."

sentences.zh: 自今已後，延至九月三十日為限。

translations.literal: From now on, the deadline is extended to the thirtieth day of the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the deadline is extended to the thirtieth day of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 」二十五年三月，敕：「關輔庸調，所稅非少，既寡蠶桑，皆資菽粟，常賤糶貴買，損費逾深。

translations.literal: " In the third month of the twenty-fifth year, an edict [stated]: "The zu-yong and diao levied in the Guanfu region are no small burden; with little mulberry and silkworm culture, all rely on beans and millet; constantly selling cheap and buying dear, the loss grows ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianbao 25 (766), an edict declared: "The zu-yong and diao levied in the Guanfu region are no light burden. With little mulberry and silkworm culture, the people rely wholly on beans and millet; constantly selling cheap and buying dear, their losses grow ever deeper."

sentences.zh: 又江淮等苦變造之勞，河路增轉輸之弊，每計其運腳，數倍加錢。

translations.literal: Moreover the Jiang-Huai region and others suffer the burden of conversion and processing; river transport adds the evils of relay shipment — counting transport costs, the cash outlay is multiplied several times over.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Huai region and others, moreover, bore the toil of conversion and processing, while river transport added the waste of relay shipment; counting transport fees alone, the cash cost was multiplied several times over.

sentences.zh: 今歲屬和平，庶物穰賤，南畝有十千之獲，京師同水火之饒，均其餘以減遠費，順其便使農無傷。

translations.literal: This year being peaceful, goods abound and prices are low; southern fields yield ten thousand [cash worth] per mu, the capital is as abundantly supplied as fire and water; apportion the surplus to reduce distant costs, follow convenience so that farmers suffer no harm.
translations.idiomatic: This year, peace prevailed, goods were plentiful and prices low, southern fields yielded ten thousand per mu, and the capital was as abundantly supplied as fire and water. Surplus should be apportioned to reduce distant costs, convenience followed so that farmers suffer no harm.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，關內諸州庸調資課，並宜準時價變粟取米，送至京逐要支用。

translations.literal: From now on, zu-yong, diao, and supplementary levies from all Guannei provinces should be converted at current prices from grain to rice and delivered to the capital for use as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, zu-yong, diao, and supplementary levies from all Guannei provinces should be converted at current prices from grain to rice and delivered to the capital for disbursement as needed.

sentences.zh: 其路遠處不可運送者，宜所在收貯，便充隨近軍糧。

translations.literal: Where distance makes delivery impossible, stores should be collected locally and used directly as rations for nearby armies.
translations.idiomatic: Where distance made delivery impossible, goods should be collected and stored locally and applied directly as rations for nearby armies.

sentences.zh: 其河南、河北有不通水利，宜折租造絹，以代關中調課。

translations.literal: For Henan and Hebei, where irrigation is lacking, rent should be converted into woven silk as substitute for the Guanzhong diao levy.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan and Hebei, where irrigation was unavailable, rent should be converted into woven silk in lieu of the Guanzhong diao levy.

sentences.zh: 所司仍明為條件，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: The responsible offices shall still set forth the regulations clearly, in accord with Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices shall set forth the regulations clearly, in accord with Our intent.
Close of edict.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年正月一日赦文：如聞百姓之內，有戶高丁多，苟為規避，父母見在，乃別籍異居。

translations.literal: Tianbao first year, first month, first day amnesty: "We have heard that among the commoners, some households are large and have many adult males; wishing to evade levies, while their parents are still living they separate registers and live apart.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty of the first day of the first month of Tianbao 1 (742): "We have heard that among the common people, some large households with many adult males, seeking to evade levies while their parents are still alive, separate registers and live apart."

sentences.zh: 宜令州縣勘會。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties should be ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties should be ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 其一家之中，有十丁已上者，放兩丁征行賦役。

translations.literal: Within one household, where there are ten adult males or more, two adult males shall be exempted from military service and labor levies.
translations.idiomatic: In households of ten adult males or more, two adult males shall be exempted from military service and labor levies.

sentences.zh: 五丁已上，放一丁。

translations.literal: Where five adult males or more, one shall be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In households of five or more, one adult male shall be exempted.

sentences.zh: 即令同籍共居，以敦風教。

translations.literal: This is to order joint registration and co-residence, to promote moral instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Households are to be kept on a single register and under one roof, to strengthen moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 其侍丁孝假，免差科。

translations.literal: For shiding filial leave, corvée and special levies are exempted.
translations.idiomatic: For shiding filial leave, corvée and special levies are exempted.

sentences.zh: 」廣德元年七月，詔：「一戶之中，三丁放一丁庸調。

translations.literal: " Guangde first year, seventh month, edict: "Within one household, for every three adult males, one is exempted from zu-yong and diao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Guangde 1 (763), an edict declared: "Within one household, for every three adult males, one is exempted from zu-yong and diao."

sentences.zh: 地稅依舊每畝稅二升。

translations.literal: Land tax remains at two sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax remained at two sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 天下男子，宜二十三成丁，五十八為老。

translations.literal: All males under Heaven should reach adult male status at twenty-three and become old at fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: All males under Heaven should reach adult-male status at twenty-three and elder status at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 」永泰元年五月，京兆麥大稔，京兆尹第五琦奏請每十畝官稅一畝，效古什一之稅。

translations.literal: " Yongtai first year, fifth month: wheat in Jingzhao had a great harvest; Jingzhao Governor Diwu Qi memorialized requesting official tax of one mu per ten mu, following the ancient one-tenth tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yongtai 1 (765), wheat in Jingzhao ripened abundantly; Jingzhao Governor Diwu Qi memorialized that the state tax one mu in ten, emulating the ancient one-tenth levy.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，諸道稅地錢使、殿中侍御史韋光裔等自諸道使還，得錢四百九十萬貫。

translations.literal: Second year, fifth month: the land-tax commissioners of the various circuits, including Palace Aide Wei Guangyi and others, returned from their circuit duties, having collected 4,900,000 strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year (766), Land-Tax Commissioner of the Various Circuits and Palace Aide Wei Guangyi and others returned from their circuit assignments having collected 4,900,000 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 乾元以來，屬天下用兵，京師百僚俸錢減耗。

translations.literal: Since Qianyuan, as the realm has been at war, the stipends of the hundred offices in the capital have been reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qianyuan (758), with the realm at war, stipends for the hundred offices in the capital had been cut.

sentences.zh: 上即位，推恩庶僚，下議公卿。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he extended grace to the common officials; the matter was deliberated by the grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor acceded, he sought to extend grace to the common officials, and the matter was debated among the grand ministers.

sentences.zh: 或以稅畝有苗者，公私鹹濟。

translations.literal: Some proposed taxing mu where seedlings had sprouted, benefiting both public and private needs alike.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed levying a tax on mu where seedlings had sprouted, which would serve both public and private needs.

sentences.zh: 乃分遣憲官，稅天下地青苗錢，以充百司課料。

translations.literal: Thereupon censorial officials were dispatched separately to levy green-sprout land tax throughout the realm, to supply the operating expenses of the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials were then dispatched separately to levy green-sprout land tax throughout the realm, to supply the operating expenses of the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 至是，仍以御史大夫為稅地錢物使，歲以為常，均給百官。

translations.literal: At this point, the Censor-in-Chief was again made Commissioner for Land-Tax Goods, made annual and regular, evenly distributed to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: At that point the Censor-in-Chief was again appointed Commissioner for Land-Tax Goods; the office was made annual and regular, with proceeds evenly distributed among the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 大曆四年正月十八日，敕有司：「定天下百姓及王公已下每年稅錢，分為九等：上上戶四千文，上中戶三千五百文，上下戶三千文。

translations.literal: Dali fourth year, eighteenth day of first month, edict to the offices: "Fix the annual tax cash for all commoners and princes and nobles down to the lowest ranks, divided into nine grades: upper-upper households 4,000 cash, upper-middle 3,500, upper-lower 3,000.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the first month of Dali 4 (769), an edict to the offices declared: "Fix the annual tax cash for all commoners and for princes and nobles down to the lowest ranks in nine grades: upper-upper households 4,000 cash, upper-middle 3,500, upper-lower 3,000."

sentences.zh: 中上戶二千五百文，中中戶二千文，中下戶一千五百文。

translations.literal: Middle-upper households 2,500 cash, middle-middle 2,000, middle-lower 1,500.
translations.idiomatic: Middle-upper households 2,500 cash, middle-middle 2,000, middle-lower 1,500.

sentences.zh: 下上戶一千文，下中戶七百文，下下戶五百文。

translations.literal: Lower-upper households 1,000 cash, lower-middle 700, lower-lower 500.
translations.idiomatic: Lower-upper households 1,000 cash, lower-middle 700, lower-lower 500.

sentences.zh: 其見官，一品准上上戶，九品准下下戶，餘品並准依此戶等稅。

translations.literal: For incumbent officials, first rank is assessed as upper-upper household, ninth rank as lower-lower household; the remaining ranks are all assessed according to these household grades.
translations.idiomatic: For incumbent officials, first rank was assessed as an upper-upper household and ninth rank as a lower-lower household; all intervening ranks were assessed according to these household grades.

sentences.zh: 若一戶數處任官，亦每處依品納稅。

translations.literal: If one household holds office in several places, at each place tax is paid according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: If a single household holds office in more than one place, tax shall be paid at each post according to official rank.

sentences.zh: 其內外官，仍據正員及占額內闕者稅。

translations.literal: As for internal and external officials, tax is still levied on the basis of regular appointments and vacancies within established quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials at court and in the provinces shall still be taxed according to their regular appointments and to vacancies within the authorized quotas.

sentences.zh: 其試及同正員文武官，不在稅限。

translations.literal: Probationary officials and civil and military officials equivalent to regular appointees are outside the tax limit.
translations.idiomatic: Probationary officials, and civil and military officers treated as equivalent to regular appointees, are not subject to this levy.

sentences.zh: 其百姓有邸店行鋪及爐冶，應准式合加本戶二等稅者，依此稅數勘責征納。

translations.literal: Commoners with inns, shops, and smelting works who under the regulations should have two grades added to their household tax shall be assessed and compelled to pay according to these tax amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners who keep inns, shops, or smelting works, and who under the regulations ought to have two household grades added to their tax, shall be audited and made to pay according to these rates.

sentences.zh: 其寄莊戶，准舊例從八等戶稅，寄住戶從九等戶稅，比類百姓，事恐不均，宜各遞加一等稅。

translations.literal: Estate-resident households, following old precedent, were taxed at the eighth grade; sojourner households at the ninth. Compared with ordinary commoners, this was likely unfair; each should be raised one grade in tax.
translations.idiomatic: Estate-resident households had been taxed at the eighth grade and sojourner households at the ninth, following old precedent. Measured against ordinary commoners, this was probably inequitable; each category should be raised one grade.

sentences.zh: 其諸色浮客及權時寄住戶等，無問有官無官，各所在為兩等收稅。

translations.literal: All kinds of floating migrants and temporary sojourners, regardless of whether they hold office, shall at each place of residence be taxed in two grades.
translations.idiomatic: All manner of floating migrants and temporary sojourners, whether they hold office or not, shall at each place of residence be taxed in two grades.

sentences.zh: 稍殷有者准八等戶，餘准九等戶。

translations.literal: Those somewhat well-off are assessed at the eighth grade; the rest at the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: Those of moderate means are assessed at the eighth grade; all others at the ninth.

sentences.zh: 如數處有莊田，亦每處稅。

translations.literal: If estate lands exist in several places, tax is levied at each place.
translations.idiomatic: If a household holds estate lands in several places, tax is levied at each.

sentences.zh: 諸道將士莊田，既緣防禦勤勞，不可同百姓例，並一切從九等輸稅。

translations.literal: Estate lands of soldiers and officers in the circuits, because of their defense duties and hardships, cannot follow the commoner precedent; all shall pay tax at the ninth grade.
translations.idiomatic: The estate lands of soldiers and officers in the circuits, given their defense duties and hardships, cannot be taxed like those of commoners; all shall pay at the ninth grade.

sentences.zh: 」其年十二月，敕：「今關輔墾田漸廣，江淮轉漕常加，計一年之儲，有太半之助，其於稅地，固可從輕。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, an edict stated: 'Cultivated land in the Guanzhong region is steadily expanding, and grain shipments from the Jiang-Huai route are constantly increasing. For the year's store of grain, more than half comes from this source. Land tax may therefore properly be reduced.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year, an edict declared: "Cultivated land in the Guanzhong region grows steadily wider, and grain transport from the Jiang-Huai route increases year by year. More than half the year's stores now come from this source. Land tax may therefore properly be lightened."

sentences.zh: 其京兆來秋稅，宜分作兩等，上下各半，上等每畝稅一斗，下等每畝稅六升。

translations.literal: For the coming autumn land tax in Jingzhao, it should be divided into two grades, upper and lower in equal proportion. Upper-grade fields shall pay one dou per mu; lower-grade fields six sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: For Jingzhao's autumn land tax next year, fields should be divided into two grades, upper and lower in equal shares: upper fields at one dou per mu, lower fields at six sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 其荒田如能佃者，宜准今年十月二十九日敕，一切每畝稅二升。

translations.literal: For wasteland that can be leased for cultivation, it should follow the edict of the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month this year: uniformly two sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Wasteland that can be brought under lease should follow the edict of the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month this year and pay uniformly two sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 仍委京兆尹及令長一一存撫，令知朕意。

translations.literal: The Jingzhao Governor and all district magistrates are further charged to care for the people in each case and make them know the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhao Governor and all district magistrates are further charged to reassure the people in each case and make them understand the throne's intent.

sentences.zh: 」五年三月，優詔定京兆府百姓稅。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, a generous edict fixed the taxes of commoners in Jingzhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year, a lenient edict fixed the taxes owed by commoners of Jingzhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夏稅，上田畝稅六升，下田畝稅四升。

translations.literal: Summer tax: upper fields six sheng per mu; lower fields four sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax: upper fields, six sheng per mu; lower fields, four sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 秋稅，上田畝稅五升，下田畝稅三升。

translations.literal: Autumn tax: upper fields five sheng per mu; lower fields three sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn tax: upper fields, five sheng per mu; lower fields, three sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 荒田開佃者，畝率二升。

translations.literal: For wasteland brought under cultivation, two sheng per mu as the rate.
translations.idiomatic: For wasteland newly brought under cultivation, the rate is two sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 八年正月二十五日，敕：「青苗地頭錢，天下每畝率十五文。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the first month of the eighth year, an edict stated: 'The green-shoot field-head levy shall be fifteen cash per mu throughout the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day of the first month of the eighth year, an edict declared: "The green-shoot field-head levy throughout the realm shall be fifteen cash per mu."

sentences.zh: 以京師煩劇，先加至三十文，自今已後，宜准諸州，每畝十五文。

translations.literal: Because the capital's burdens are heavy, it had previously been raised to thirty cash. From now on it should follow the other prefectures: fifteen cash per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Because the capital's burdens are heavy, the levy there had first been raised to thirty cash. Henceforth it should follow the other prefectures at fifteen cash per mu.
Close of edict.

sentences.zh: 建中元年二月，遣黜陟使分行天下，其詔略曰：「戶無主客，以見居為簿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jianzhong, imperial envoys for promotion and demotion were dispatched throughout the realm. The edict in summary stated: 'Household registers shall make no distinction between native and guest status; registration shall follow current residence.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Jianzhong (780), imperial envoys for promotion and demotion were dispatched throughout the realm. The edict in summary declared: "Household registers shall make no distinction between native and guest status; registration shall follow current residence."

sentences.zh: 人無丁中，以貧富為差。

translations.literal: No distinction shall be made among people by adult-male status; differentiation shall be by wealth and poverty.
translations.idiomatic: No distinction shall be made among people by adult-male status; differentiation shall be by wealth and poverty.

sentences.zh: 行商者，在郡縣稅三十之一。

translations.literal: Traveling merchants shall be taxed one-thirtieth at the commandery and county.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling merchants shall pay a tax of one-thirtieth at the commandery and county.

sentences.zh: 居人之稅，秋夏兩征之。

translations.literal: Tax on residents shall be collected in both autumn and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Tax on residents shall be collected in both autumn and summer.

sentences.zh: 各有不便者，三之。

translations.literal: Those for whom this presents hardship shall pay in three installments.
translations.idiomatic: Those for whom this is inconvenient may pay in three installments.

sentences.zh: 餘征賦悉罷，而丁額不廢。

translations.literal: All other levies are abolished, but the adult-male register is not discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: All other levies are abolished, but the adult-male register is not discontinued.

sentences.zh: 其田畝之稅，率以大曆十四年墾數為准。

translations.literal: Land tax per mu shall be reckoned on the basis of cultivated land figures from the fourteenth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax per mu shall be reckoned on the basis of cultivated land figures from the fourteenth year of Dali (779).

sentences.zh: 征夏稅無過六月。

translations.literal: Summer tax collection shall not extend beyond the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax shall be collected no later than the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 秋稅無過十一月。

translations.literal: Autumn tax shall not extend beyond the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn tax shall be collected no later than the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 違者進退長吏。

translations.literal: Violators shall be subject to demotion or removal of the chief local official.
translations.idiomatic: Violators shall be subject to demotion or removal of the responsible chief local official.

sentences.zh: 令黜陟使各量風土所宜、人戶多少均之，定其賦，尚書度支總統焉。

translations.literal: Let each imperial envoy, according to local conditions and the number of households, equalize the burden and fix the levy; the Ministry of Revenue shall supervise all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Let each imperial envoy, according to local conditions and the number of households, equalize the burden and fix the levy; the Ministry of Revenue shall supervise the whole.

sentences.zh: 」三年五月，淮南節度使陳少游請於本道兩稅錢每千增二百，因詔他州悉如之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, Chen Shaoyou, Military Commissioner of Huainan, requested that the dual-tax cash levy in his circuit be increased by two hundred per thousand; an edict ordered all other prefectures to follow suit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year, Chen Shaoyou, Military Commissioner of Huainan, requested that the dual-tax cash levy in his circuit be increased by two hundred per thousand; an edict ordered all other circuits to do the same.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，劍南西川觀察使韋皋奏請加稅什二，以增給官吏，從之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Wei Gao, Surveillance Commissioner of western Sichuan, memorialized requesting a twenty-percent tax increase to supplement officials' stipends; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Wei Gao, Surveillance Commissioner of western Sichuan, memorialized requesting a twenty-percent tax increase to supplement officials' stipends; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年八月，中書門下奏：「伏准今年閏正月十七日敕，令百僚議錢貨輕重者，今據群官楊於陵等議，'伏請天下兩稅榷鹽酒利等，悉以布帛絲綿，任土所產物充稅，並不征見錢，則物漸重，錢漸輕，農人見免賤賣匹帛'者。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: 'We respectfully note the edict of the seventeenth day of the intercalary first month this year, ordering the hundred officials to debate the relative weight of coin and goods. Now, according to the deliberations of the assembled officials Yang Yuling and others: "We respectfully request that throughout the realm the dual tax, salt monopoly, wine monopoly, and similar revenues all be paid in cloth, silk, and floss — whatever local products yield — as tax, with no collection of cash coin; then goods will gradually gain weight, coin will gradually lose weight, and farmers will be spared selling silk and cloth at depressed prices."'
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe (820), the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "We respectfully note the edict of the seventeenth day of the intercalary first month this year, ordering the hundred officials to debate the relative weight of coin and goods. Now, according to the deliberations of the assembled officials Yang Yuling and others — 'We respectfully request that throughout the realm the dual tax, salt monopoly, wine monopoly, and similar revenues all be paid in cloth, silk, and floss, whatever local products yield, with no collection of cash coin; then goods will gradually gain weight, coin will gradually lose weight, and farmers will be spared selling silk and cloth at depressed prices' —"

sentences.zh: 伏以群臣所議，事皆至當，深利公私。

translations.literal: We respectfully consider that what the ministers have proposed is entirely appropriate and greatly benefits both public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully consider that what the ministers have proposed is entirely appropriate and greatly benefits both public and private interests.

sentences.zh: 請商量付度支，據諸州府應徵兩稅，供上都及留州留使舊額。

translations.literal: We request that deliberation be entrusted to the Ministry of Revenue, calculating from the dual tax collected by each prefecture and circuit the amounts due to the capital and the fixed amounts retained locally by prefecture and commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: We request that deliberation be entrusted to the Ministry of Revenue, calculating from the dual tax collected by each prefecture and circuit the amounts due to the capital and the fixed amounts retained locally by prefecture and commissioner.

sentences.zh: 起元和十六年已後，並改配端匹斤兩之物為稅額，如大曆已前租庸課調，不計錢，令其折納。

translations.literal: Beginning from the sixteenth year of Yuanhe onward, tax quotas shall all be reassigned as measured items of bolts, rolls, and weight; as with the zu-yong and tiao levies before Dali, without reckoning in cash — requiring conversion payments.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning from the sixteenth year of Yuanhe onward, tax quotas shall all be reassigned as measured goods in bolts, rolls, and weight; as with the zu-yong and tiao levies before Dali, without reckoning in cash — requiring commutation in kind.

sentences.zh: 使人知定制，供辦有常。

translations.literal: This will let people know fixed quotas, and supply will be reliably provided.
translations.idiomatic: This will let people know fixed quotas, and supply will be reliably provided.

sentences.zh: 仍約元和十五年征納布帛等估價。

translations.literal: Valuations for cloth and silk collected in the fifteenth year of Yuanhe shall still serve as the basis.
translations.idiomatic: Valuations for cloth and silk collected in the fifteenth year of Yuanhe shall still serve as the basis.

sentences.zh: 其舊納虛估物，與依虛估物回計，如舊納實估物並見錢，即當於端匹斤兩上量加估價回計。

translations.literal: Where payment had been in goods at inflated valuation, convert according to inflated valuation; where payment had been in goods at actual valuation together with cash, the added valuation shall be reckoned on the bolts, rolls, and weight measures.
translations.idiomatic: Where payment had been in goods at inflated valuation, convert according to inflated valuation; where payment had been in goods at actual valuation together with cash, the added valuation shall be reckoned on the bolts, rolls, and weight measures.

sentences.zh: 變法在長其物價，價長則永利公私。

translations.literal: The purpose of changing the law is to raise the price of goods; when prices rise, the benefit to public and private alike will be lasting.
translations.idiomatic: The purpose of changing the law is to raise the price of goods; when prices rise, the benefit to public and private alike will be lasting.

sentences.zh: 初雖微有加饒，法行即當就實。

translations.literal: At first there may be a slight excess allowance, but once the law is in force it will settle to actual amounts.
translations.idiomatic: At first there may be a slight excess allowance, but once the law is in force it will settle to actual amounts.

sentences.zh: 比舊給用，固利而不害。

translations.literal: Compared with past disbursements, this is plainly beneficial and harmless.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with past disbursements, this is plainly beneficial and harmless.

sentences.zh: 仍作條件處置，編入旨符。

translations.literal: Detailed provisions shall still be drawn up and compiled into imperial directives.
translations.idiomatic: Detailed provisions shall still be drawn up and compiled into imperial directives.

sentences.zh: 其鹽利酒利，本以榷率計錢，有殊兩稅之名，不可除去錢額。

translations.literal: Salt and wine monopoly profits are originally calculated at monopoly rates in cash; their designation differs from the dual tax, and the cash amounts cannot be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and wine monopoly profits are originally calculated at monopoly rates in cash; their designation differs from the dual tax, and the cash amounts cannot be removed.

sentences.zh: 中有令納見錢者，亦請令折納時估匹段。

translations.literal: Where payment in cash is prescribed, we also request that conversion at current valuation in bolts of cloth be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Where payment in cash is prescribed, we also request that conversion at current valuation in bolts of cloth be permitted.

sentences.zh: 上既不專以錢為稅，人得以所產輸官，錢貨必均其重輕，隴畝自廣於蠶織。

translations.literal: Since the throne will no longer rely exclusively on coin as tax, people may submit what their land produces to the state. Coin and goods will inevitably reach a balanced weight, and fields and homesteads will naturally broaden sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Since the throne will no longer rely exclusively on coin as tax, people may submit what their land produces to the state. Coin and goods will inevitably reach a balanced weight, and fields and homesteads will naturally broaden sericulture.

sentences.zh: 便時惠下，庶得其宜。

translations.literal: Timely relief for the people below — this may achieve what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Timely relief for the people below — this may achieve what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 其土乏絲麻，或地連邊塞，風俗更異，賦入不同，亦請商量，委所司裁酌，隨便宜處置。

translations.literal: Where the soil lacks silk and hemp, or the land adjoins the frontier and local customs differ, so that revenue differs — we also request deliberation, delegated to the responsible offices to determine as local convenience permits.
translations.idiomatic: Where the soil lacks silk and hemp, or the land adjoins the frontier and local customs differ, so that revenue differs — we also request deliberation, delegated to the responsible offices to determine as local convenience permits.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 大和四年五月，劍南西川宣撫使、諫議大夫崔戎奏：「准詔旨制置西川事條。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Dahe, Cui Rong, Pacification Commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit and Remonstrance Grand Master, memorialized: "In accordance with the edict's provisions for arranging affairs in Western Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Dahe 4 (830), Cui Rong, Pacification Commissioner for Western Sichuan in Jiannan and Remonstrance Grand Master, submitted a memorial: "Pursuant to the imperial edict governing the administration of Western Sichuan,

sentences.zh: 今與郭釗商量，兩稅錢數內三分，二分納見錢，一分折納匹段，每二貫加饒百姓五百文，計一十三萬四千二百四十三貫文。

translations.literal: Having now consulted with Guo Zhao, within the Two-Tax levy, of three parts, two parts are paid in cash and one part converted to bolts of cloth; for every two strings an extra five hundred cash is granted in favor of the people, totaling one hundred thirty-four thousand two hundred forty-three strings.
translations.idiomatic: I have consulted with Guo Zhao. Of the Two-Tax revenue, two-thirds shall be collected in coin and one-third in converted cloth payments; for every two strings collected, the people receive an additional concession of five hundred cash—amounting to 134,243 strings in all.

sentences.zh: 依此曉諭百姓訖。

translations.literal: The people have been instructed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The populace has been notified of these terms.

sentences.zh: 經賊州縣，准詔三分減放一分，計減錢六萬七千六百二十貫文。

translations.literal: In prefectures and counties that suffered banditry, in accordance with the edict one part in three of the levy was reduced and remitted, totaling a reduction of sixty-seven thousand six hundred twenty strings.
translations.idiomatic: In districts ravaged by bandits, one-third of the levy was reduced and remitted as the edict prescribed, for a total reduction of 67,620 strings.

sentences.zh: 不經賊處，先征見錢，今三分一分折納雜物，計優饒百姓一十三萬貫。

translations.literal: In places not touched by bandits, cash had been collected first; now one part in three may be converted to miscellaneous goods in payment, benefiting the people by one hundred thirty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: In districts untouched by bandits, where cash had previously been collected in full, one-third may now be paid in converted goods—a benefit to the people worth 130,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 舊有稅薑芋之類，每畝至七八百。

translations.literal: There were formerly taxes on ginger, taro, and the like, reaching seven or eight hundred per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes on ginger, taro, and similar crops had formerly run as high as seven or eight hundred cash per mu.

sentences.zh: 征斂不時，今並省稅名，盡依諸處為四限等第，先給戶帖，餘一切名目勒停。

translations.literal: Collection was untimely; now all such tax names are abolished, and everything follows the four-tier gradations used elsewhere; household registers are issued first, and all remaining impost names are strictly suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Because collection had been irregular, those tax categories have all been abolished. Assessments now follow the four-tier gradations used elsewhere; household tax registers are issued first, and every remaining levy name is suspended.
Close of edict.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，仍用隋之五銖錢。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he continued to use the Sui dynasty's five-zhu coins.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he continued to use the Sui five-zhu coin.

sentences.zh: 武德四年七月，廢五銖錢，行開元通寶錢，徑八分，重二銖四絫，積十文重一兩。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Wude, the five-zhu coin was abolished and the Kaiyuan tongbao coin was put into circulation; diameter eight fen, weight two zhu four lei; ten coins together weighed one liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Wude 4 (621), the five-zhu coin was abolished and the Kaiyuan tongbao introduced—eight fen in diameter, two zhu four lei in weight, ten coins to the liang.

sentences.zh: 一千文重六斤四兩。

translations.literal: One thousand coins weighed six jin four liang.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand coins weighed six jin and four liang.

sentences.zh: 仍置錢監於洛、並、幽、益等州。

translations.literal: Mint supervisors were also established in Luoyang, Bing, You, Yi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Mint supervisors were also established at Luoyang, Bing, You, Yi, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 秦王、齊王各賜三爐鑄錢，右僕射裴寂賜一爐。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin and the Prince of Qi were each granted three furnaces for casting coin; the Right Vice Director Pei Ji was granted one furnace.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin and the Prince of Qi were each granted three minting furnaces; Pei Ji, Vice Director of the Right, received one.

sentences.zh: 敢有盜鑄者身死，家口配沒。

translations.literal: Whoever dared illicitly to cast coin would be executed, and his household registered for penal servitude and confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who dared cast coin illicitly would be put to death, his household registered for penal servitude and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，又于桂州置監。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, a supervisor was also established at Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year, a mint supervisor was also established at Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 議者以新錢輕重大小最為折衷，遠近甚便之。

translations.literal: Commentators held that the new coin's weight and size were the most balanced compromise, greatly convenient near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Observers judged the new coin's weight and size the happiest medium, and found it greatly convenient throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 後盜鑄漸起，而所在用錢濫惡。
