translations.literal: Later illicit casting gradually arose, and the coins in use everywhere became debased and poor.
translations.idiomatic: Later illicit casting spread, and coin in circulation everywhere grew debased and wretched.

sentences.zh: 顯慶五年九月，敕以惡錢轉多，令所在官私為市取，以五惡錢酬一好錢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Xianqing, an edict was issued because debased coin was growing numerous, ordering that wherever official and private parties traded in the market, five debased coins would be exchanged for one good coin.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Xianqing 5 (660), an edict declared that debased coin had grown too common and ordered that in all market transactions, public and private alike, five debased coins be taken for one good coin.

sentences.zh: 百姓以惡錢價賤，私自藏之，以候官禁之弛。

translations.literal: The people, because debased coin was cheap in value, secretly hoarded it, waiting for the official prohibition to relax.
translations.idiomatic: Because debased coin fetched so little, the people hoarded it in secret, waiting for the ban to lapse.

sentences.zh: 高宗又令以好錢一文買惡錢兩文，弊仍不息。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong also ordered that one good coin could buy two debased coins, yet the abuse still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong then ordered that one good coin could purchase two debased ones—but the abuse only continued.

sentences.zh: 至乾封元年封嶽之後，又改造新錢，文曰「乾封泉寶」，徑一寸，重二銖六分，仍與舊錢並行。

translations.literal: When the first year of Qianfeng came, after the fengshan ceremony, new coin was again cast, inscribed "Qianfeng quanbao," one cun in diameter, weighing two zhu six fen, still circulating alongside the old coin.
translations.idiomatic: After the fengshan rite at Mount Tai in Qianfeng 1 (666), new coin was cast bearing the inscription "Qianfeng quanbao"—one cun across, two zhu six fen in weight—circulating alongside the old coin.

sentences.zh: 新錢一文當舊錢之十。

translations.literal: One new coin was equivalent to ten old coins.
translations.idiomatic: One new coin counted for ten of the old.

sentences.zh: 周年之後，舊錢並廢。

translations.literal: After a full year, the old coin was altogether abolished.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, the old coin was abolished entirely.

sentences.zh: 初，開元錢之文，給事中歐陽詢制詞及書，時稱其工。

translations.literal: Initially, the inscription on the Kaiyuan coin—the wording composed and calligraphy written by Supervising Secretary Ouyang Xun—was at the time praised for its craftsmanship.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan coin's legend had been composed and inscribed by Ouyang Xun, Supervising Secretary—a work then widely admired for its artistry.

sentences.zh: 其字含八分及隸體，其詞先上後下，次左後右讀之。

translations.literal: Its characters combined bafen and clerical script forms; the wording was read first top then bottom, then left then right.
translations.idiomatic: The characters blended bafen and clerical styles; the legend was read top to bottom, then left to right.

sentences.zh: 自上及左回環讀之，其義亦通。

translations.literal: Read in circuit from top to left, the meaning also held.
translations.idiomatic: Read in a circuit from the top around to the left, the sense still held.

sentences.zh: 流俗謂之開通元寶錢。

translations.literal: Among the populace it was called the Kaitong yuanbao coin.
translations.idiomatic: Among common folk it was called the Kaitong yuanbao coin.

sentences.zh: 及鑄新錢，乃同流俗，「乾」字直上，「封」字在左。

translations.literal: When the new coin was cast, it followed popular usage: the character Qian stood upright at top, and Feng at left.
translations.idiomatic: When the new coin was cast, the minters followed popular usage instead: Qian upright at the top, Feng to the left.

sentences.zh: 尋寤錢文之誤，又緣改鑄，商賈不通，米帛增價，乃議卻用舊錢。

translations.literal: Soon the error in the coin inscription was perceived; also because of the recasting, merchants could not trade freely, and grain and silk rose in price—thereupon it was proposed to revert to the old coin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the error in the coin legend was recognized. The recoinage had also choked commerce and driven up the price of grain and silk, and the court began to debate a return to the old coin.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，下詔曰：「泉布之興，其來自久。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, an edict was issued: The rise of currency—its origin is long ago.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, an edict declared: Coinage is no recent invention.

sentences.zh: 實古今之要重，為公私之寶用。

translations.literal: It is truly weighty through past and present, a treasure for public and private use.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present it has been indispensable—a treasure alike to the state and to private households.

sentences.zh: 年月既深，偽濫斯起，所以采乾封之號，改鑄新錢。

translations.literal: As years and months grew deep, counterfeiting and debasement arose; therefore the Qianfeng title was adopted and new coin recast.
translations.idiomatic: But as time wore on, counterfeiting and debasement multiplied—hence the Qianfeng name was taken and new coin struck.

sentences.zh: 靜而思之，將為未可。

translations.literal: When pondered in quiet, this will prove inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: On sober reflection, this course will not do.

sentences.zh: 高祖撥亂反正，爰創軌模。

translations.literal: Gaozu settled chaos and restored order, therein establishing the model.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu quelled the chaos of the age and restored order, laying down the pattern for the realm.

sentences.zh: 太宗立極承天，無所改作。

translations.literal: Taizong took the pinnacle and received Heaven's mandate, altering nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ascended the throne in accord with Heaven and changed nothing that need not be changed.

sentences.zh: 今廢舊造新，恐乖先旨。

translations.literal: Now to abolish the old and create the new—we fear this strays from the earlier intent.
translations.idiomatic: To discard the old and mint anew now would, we fear, betray their intent.

sentences.zh: 其開元通寶，宜依舊施行，為萬代之法。

translations.literal: The Kaiyuan tongbao should be implemented as before, as the law for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan tongbao should remain in force as before—a standard for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 乾封新鑄之錢，令所司貯納，更不須鑄。

translations.literal: The newly cast Qianfeng coins—let the responsible offices store them; no further casting is required.
translations.idiomatic: The newly minted Qianfeng coin shall be stored by the responsible offices, and no more of it shall be cast.

sentences.zh: 仍令天下置爐之處，並鑄開元通寶錢。

translations.literal: Also order that everywhere in the realm where furnaces are established, Kaiyuan tongbao coins shall be cast.
translations.idiomatic: Every mint in the realm shall resume casting Kaiyuan tongbao coin.

sentences.zh: 」既而私鑄更多，錢復濫惡。

translations.literal: " Thereafter private casting increased further, and coin again became debased.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter private casting increased further, and coin again became debased.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗臨軒謂侍臣曰：「錢之為用，行之已久，公私要便，莫甚於斯。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong once faced the hall and said to attending ministers: The use of coin has been practiced long; for public and private convenience, nothing surpasses it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong once addressed his ministers from the throne: Coin has long been in use—nothing serves public and private need so well.

sentences.zh: 比為州縣不存檢校，私鑄過多。

translations.literal: Recently because prefectures and counties have not maintained inspection, private casting has been excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, because prefectures and counties have failed to enforce oversight, private casting has grown rampant.

sentences.zh: 如聞荊、潭、宣、衡，犯法尤甚。

translations.literal: As I have heard, Jing, Tan, Xuan, and Heng have been especially severe in violating the law.
translations.idiomatic: I am told that Jing, Tan, Xuan, and Heng have been worst of all in breaking the law.

sentences.zh: 遂有將船筏宿于江中，所部官人不能覺察。

translations.literal: Thereupon some have kept boats and rafts moored in the river, which officials under their jurisdiction cannot detect.
translations.idiomatic: Some have taken to anchoring boats and rafts mid-river to cast coin, beyond the reach of local officials.

sentences.zh: 自今嚴加禁斷，所在追納惡錢，一二年間使盡。

translations.literal: From now on strictly prohibit this; everywhere pursue and collect debased coin, so that within one or two years they are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the ban must be enforced without mercy. Debased coin shall be hunted down and collected everywhere until, within a year or two, none remains.

sentences.zh: 」當時雖有約敕，而奸濫不息。

translations.literal: " At the time, though there were binding edicts, crafty abuse did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Though binding edicts were in force, crafty abuse did not cease.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳四年四月，令東都出遠年糙米及粟，就市給糶，鬥別納惡錢百文。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Yifeng, the Eastern Capital was ordered to release aged coarse rice and millet, selling it in the markets, accepting one hundred debased coins per dou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yifeng 4 (679), the Eastern Capital was ordered to release old coarse rice and millet for sale in the markets, accepting one hundred debased coins per dou.

sentences.zh: 其惡錢令少府司農相知，即令鑄破。

translations.literal: Those debased coins were ordered to be communicated between the Palace Privy and the Minister of Finance for mutual awareness, and immediately cast and broken up.
translations.idiomatic: The debased coin thus collected was to be reported to both the Palace Treasury and the Ministry of Revenue, then immediately recast and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其厚重徑合斤兩者，任將行用，時米粟漸貴，議者以為鑄錢漸多，所以錢賤而物貴。

translations.literal: Those that were heavy, thick, and in diameter conformed to the standard weight—such were permitted to continue in circulation; at the time grain and millet gradually grew expensive, and observers held that because coin casting was gradually increasing, money was cheap while goods were dear.
translations.idiomatic: Coin that was heavy, thick, and true to the standard weight and measure might still circulate. Grain and millet were meanwhile growing dear, and commentators blamed the steady increase in minting: too much coin, too little goods.

sentences.zh: 於是權停少府監鑄錢，尋而復舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Palace Privy mint's coin casting was temporarily halted; soon it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Treasury mint was therefore suspended for a time—only to resume before long.

sentences.zh: 則天長安中，又令懸樣於市，令百姓依樣用錢。

translations.literal: In Wu Zetian's Chang'an reign, again ordered samples hung in the markets, ordering the common people to use coins according to the samples.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an reign of Empress Wu, the court again posted sample coins in the markets and ordered the people to circulate cash only according to those models.

sentences.zh: 俄又簡擇艱難，交易留滯。

translations.literal: Before long, screening again grew difficult, and exchange stagnated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, inspection and sorting grew onerous again, and trade stalled.

sentences.zh: 又降敕非鐵錫、銅蕩、穿穴者，並許行用。

translations.literal: Again an edict was issued: except iron-tin, worn copper, and drilled coins, all were permitted for circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared that every coin might circulate except those of iron-and-tin alloy, worn-down copper, or punched with holes.

sentences.zh: 其有熟銅、排鬥、沙澀、厚大者，皆不許簡。

translations.literal: As to those of refined copper, matched-mold castings, gritty sand-cast pieces, and thick oversized coins, all were not permitted to be screened out.
translations.idiomatic: Coins of fine copper, matched-mold counterfeits, gritty sand-cast pieces, and thick oversized pieces — none of these might be rejected in inspection.

sentences.zh: 自是盜鑄蜂起，濫惡益眾。

translations.literal: From this, counterfeiting swarmed like bees, and debased inferior coins grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiting then swarmed like bees, and debased coinage grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 江淮之南，盜鑄者或就陂湖、巨海、深山之中，波濤險峻，人跡罕到，州縣莫能禁約。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi and Huai, counterfeiters sometimes went to lakes, great seas, and deep mountains — treacherous waves, steep peril, places human footsteps rarely reached — and prefectures and counties could not forbid or restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi and Huai, counterfeiters worked from lake country, open sea, and deep mountains — places of steep coasts and treacherous waters, where human feet rarely trod and where prefectures and counties could not reach to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 以至神龍、先天之際，兩京用錢尤濫。

translations.literal: Reaching the Shenlong and Xiantian periods, coin use in the two capitals was especially debased.
translations.idiomatic: By the Shenlong and Xiantian eras, currency in the two capitals had grown especially debased.

sentences.zh: 其郴、衡私鑄小錢，才有輪郭，及鐵錫五銖之屬，亦堪行用。

translations.literal: In Chen and Heng, privately cast small coins having only rims, and iron-tin five-zhu types and the like, were also fit for circulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenzhou and Hengzhou, privately cast small coins barely bearing a rim, along with iron-tin pieces and imitations of the five-zhu — all passed for good money.

sentences.zh: 乃有買錫熔銷，以錢模夾之，斯須則盈千百，便齎用之。

translations.literal: Thereupon some bought tin and melted it, clamped it in coin molds, and in an instant filled hundreds and thousands, then immediately carried them for use.
translations.idiomatic: Some bought tin, melted it down, squeezed it in coin molds, and in moments produced hundreds or thousands of pieces ready to spend.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，車駕往東都，宋璟知政事，奏請一切禁斷惡錢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, the imperial carriage went to the Eastern Capital; Song Jing directed affairs of state and memorialized requesting total prohibition and cutting off of debased coins.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 5 (717), when the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital, Song Jing, heading the chief council, memorialized asking that debased coinage be banned outright.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，又切斷天下惡錢，行二銖四絫錢。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, again strictly cut off debased coins under Heaven, circulating coins of two zhu four lei weight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kaiyuan 6 (718), the court again ordered a nationwide purge of debased coin and enforced the standard of two zhu four lei per coin.

sentences.zh: 不堪行用者，並銷破復鑄。

translations.literal: Those unfit for circulation were all melted down and recast.
translations.idiomatic: Coins unfit for circulation were all melted and recast.

sentences.zh: 至二月又敕曰：「古者聚萬方之貨，設九府之法，以通天下，以便生人。

translations.literal: By the second month another edict said: "In antiquity, gathering the goods of ten thousand regions, establishing the law of the nine treasuries, to circulate under Heaven and benefit the living.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month another edict declared: "In antiquity the kings gathered goods from every quarter and established the nine-treasury system to circulate wealth across the realm and ease the lives of the people.

sentences.zh: 若輕重得中，則利可知矣；

translations.literal: If light and heavy obtain the mean, then benefit may be known;
translations.idiomatic: When weight and value hold true to the mean, the public good is clear;

sentences.zh: 若真偽相雜，則官失其守。

translations.literal: if true and false are mixed, then the office loses its guard.
translations.idiomatic: when genuine and counterfeit mingle, the state loses control of the currency.

sentences.zh: 頃者用錢，不論此道。

translations.literal: Recently in coin use, this principle was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years coinage has ignored this principle entirely.

sentences.zh: 深恐貧窶日困，奸豪歲滋。

translations.literal: Deeply fearing the poor daily grow distressed, the cunning and powerful yearly increase.
translations.idiomatic: We greatly fear that the poor grow poorer by the day and the unscrupulous wax stronger year by year.

sentences.zh: 所以申明舊章，懸設諸樣，欲其人安俗阜，禁止令行。

translations.literal: Therefore clarifying old statutes, hanging up various samples, wishing the people secure and customs prosperous, prohibition and orders enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we have clarified the old statutes and posted sample coins, seeking peace for the people, prosperity for custom, and strict enforcement of the ban.

sentences.zh: 」時江淮錢尤濫惡，有官爐、偏爐、棱錢、時錢等數色。

translations.literal: " At the time Jiang-Huai coin was especially debased, with several kinds such as official-furnace, side-furnace, rim-coin, and current-coin.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jiang-Huai coinage was especially debased — official-mint, side-mint, rim-weighted, and current-cast pieces, in several distinct sorts.

sentences.zh: 璟乃遣監察御史蕭隱之充江淮使。

translations.literal: Jing then dispatched Investigating Censor Xiao Yinzhí to serve as Jianghuai commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing dispatched Investigating Censor Xiao Yinzhí as commissioner for the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 隱之乃令率戶出錢，務加督責。

translations.literal: Yinzhí then ordered every household to produce coins, zealously adding supervision and demands.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhí ordered every household to turn in coin and pressed the mandate relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 百姓乃以上青錢充惡錢納之，其小惡者或沉之於江湖，以免罪戾。

translations.literal: The common people then substituted high-quality green coins for debased coins in surrendering them; small debased ones they sometimes sank in rivers and lakes to escape guilt and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The people substituted fine bronze coin for debased coin in what they surrendered; the worst pieces they sometimes sank in rivers and lakes to escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 於是市井不通，物價騰起，流聞京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon market traffic did not circulate, prices of goods soared, and the report reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Markets seized up, prices soared, and word reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 隱之貶官，璟因之罷相，乃以張嘉貞知政事。

translations.literal: Yinzhí was demoted in office; Jing was removed as chief minister; then Zhang Jiuzhen was put in charge of affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhí was demoted, Song Jing was dismissed as chief minister, and Zhang Jiuzhen took charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞乃弛其禁，人乃安之。

translations.literal: Jiuzhen then relaxed the prohibition, and the people were then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuzhen eased the ban, and the people settled down again.

sentences.zh: 開元二十二年，中書侍郎張九齡初知政事，奏請不禁鑄錢，玄宗令百官詳議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan, Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Jiuling first directed affairs of state and memorialized requesting not to forbid coin casting; Xuanzong ordered the hundred officials to discuss in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 22 (734), Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Jiuling newly joined the chief council and memorialized to lift the ban on private minting; Xuanzong ordered the full court to debate the proposal.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎裴耀卿李林甫、河南少尹蕭炅等皆曰：「錢者通貨，有國之權，是以歷代禁之，以絕奸濫。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Pei Yaoxing, Li Linfu, Henan Assistant Director Xiao Jiong and others all said: "Coin is circulating currency, the power of a state; therefore every generation forbade it, to cut off crafty abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Chancellery Pei Yaoxing, Li Linfu, Henan Assistant Director Xiao Jiong, and others argued: "Cash is the medium of exchange and an instrument of sovereign power; every dynasty has therefore forbidden private minting to choke off fraud and debasement.

sentences.zh: 今若一啟此門，但恐小人棄農逐利，而濫惡更甚，於事不便。

translations.literal: Now if once opening this gate, only fearing petty men abandoning farming to pursue profit, while debased inferior becomes still worse — on the affair not convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Open that door even once, and small men will abandon the plow for profit while debased coin grows worse still — the harm is plain.

sentences.zh: 」左監門錄事參軍劉秩上議曰：

translations.literal: " Left Supervisor of the Gate Clerical Registrar Liu Zhi presented a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Left Gate Guard Clerical Registrar Liu Zhi submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 伏奉今月二十一日敕，欲不禁鑄錢，令百僚詳議可否者。

translations.literal: Humbly receiving this month's twenty-first day edict, wishing not to forbid coin casting, ordering the hundred officials to discuss in detail whether feasible or not.
translations.idiomatic: I have received the edict of the twenty-first of this month proposing to lift the ban on private minting and asking the full court to weigh its wisdom.

sentences.zh: 夫錢之興，其來尚矣，將以平輕重而權本末。

translations.literal: As to the rise of coin, its coming is long; it will use this to balance light and heavy and weigh root and branch.
translations.idiomatic: Coinage is of ancient origin; it exists to balance weight and value and to mediate between primary and secondary goods.

sentences.zh: 齊桓得其術而國以霸，周景失其道而人用弊。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi obtained its art and the state thereby hegemonized; King Jing of Zhou lost its way and the people used debased coin.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi mastered this art and his state rose to hegemony; King Jing of Zhou lost it and his people were left with worthless coin.

sentences.zh: 考諸載籍，國之興衰，實系於是。

translations.literal: Examining the records, the rise and fall of states truly hangs on this.
translations.idiomatic: The historical record shows that dynastic rise and fall truly hinge on this.

sentences.zh: 陛下思變古以濟今，欲反經以合道，而不即改作，詢之芻堯，臣雖蠢愚，敢不薦其聞見。

translations.literal: Your Majesty thinks to change antiquity to aid the present, wishes to reverse the classic to accord with the Way, yet not immediately reforming, inquiring of grass and firewood gatherers — though your subject is dull and foolish, how dare he not offer what he has heard and seen.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty seeks to adapt ancient ways to present needs and bend established principle to fit the Way, yet rather than act at once you consult even humble commoners — though I am slow-witted, how could I withhold what I know?

sentences.zh: 古者以珠玉為上幣，黃金為中幣，刀布為下幣。

translations.literal: In antiquity, pearls and jade were upper coin, gold middle coin, knife and cloth lower coin.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity pearls and jade served as supreme currency, gold as medium currency, and knives and cloth as common currency.

sentences.zh: 管仲曰：「夫三幣，握之則非有補於暖也，舍之則非有損於飽也。

translations.literal: Guan Zhong said: "As to the three coins, held in the hand they do not add to warmth; set aside they do not diminish satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said: "These three currencies — clutched in the hand they do not warm you; laid aside they do not leave you hungry.

sentences.zh: 先王以守財物，以禦人事，而平天下也。

translations.literal: The former kings used them to guard wealth and goods, to control human affairs, and to balance the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings used them to safeguard stored wealth, to govern human affairs, and to balance the realm.

sentences.zh: 」是以命之曰衡。

translations.literal: " Therefore they named it Balance.
translations.idiomatic: Hence they called this the Balance.

sentences.zh: 衡者，使物一高一下，不得有常。

translations.literal: Balance means making goods one moment high, one moment low, not allowed to have constancy.
translations.idiomatic: The Balance means letting the value of goods rise and fall — never fixed at one level.

sentences.zh: 故與之在君，奪之在君，貧之在君，富之在君。

translations.literal: Therefore giving rests with the ruler, taking rests with the ruler, impoverishing rests with the ruler, enriching rests with the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: To give rests with the ruler, to take rests with the ruler, to impoverish rests with the ruler, to enrich rests with the ruler.

sentences.zh: 是以人戴君如日月，親君如父母，用此術也。

translations.literal: Therefore people revere the ruler as sun and moon, are close to the ruler as to parents — using this art.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the people revere their ruler as they do the sun and moon and love him as they do their parents — by this art alone.

sentences.zh: 是為人主之權。

translations.literal: This is the ruler's power.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the sovereign's power.

sentences.zh: 今之錢，即古之下幣也。

translations.literal: Today's coin is antiquity's lower coin.
translations.idiomatic: Today's cash is the common currency of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 陛下若舍之任人，則上無以禦下，下無以事上，其不可一也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty abandons it and leaves it to men, then above there is no means to control below, below no means to serve above — the first impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty leaves coinage to private hands, then the throne loses leverage over the people and the people lose the means to serve the throne — that is the first reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 夫物賤則傷農，錢輕則傷賈。

translations.literal: When goods are cheap then farmers are harmed; when coin is light then merchants are harmed.
translations.idiomatic: When goods are cheap, farmers suffer; when coin is light, merchants suffer.

sentences.zh: 故善為國者，觀物之貴賤，錢之輕重。

translations.literal: Therefore one who skillfully governs a state observes the dearth and cheapness of goods, the light and heavy of coin.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled ruler watches the price of goods and the weight of coin alike.

sentences.zh: 夫物重則錢輕，錢輕由乎物多，多則作法收之使少；

translations.literal: When goods are heavy then coin is light; coin is light because goods are many — when many, then by method collect them to make few;
translations.idiomatic: When goods are plentiful, coin grows light; when goods abound, policy must absorb them to restore scarcity;

sentences.zh: 少則重，重則作法布之使輕。

translations.literal: when few then heavy, when heavy then by method distribute to make light.
translations.idiomatic: when goods are scarce they grow costly, and costly goods must be released to make them cheap again.

sentences.zh: 輕重之本，必由乎是，奈何而假於人？

translations.literal: The root of light and heavy must lie in this — how then lend it to other men?
translations.idiomatic: The root of monetary balance lies here — how then can it be entrusted to private men?

sentences.zh: 其不可二也。

translations.literal: Its second impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 夫鑄錢不雜以鉛鐵則無利，雜以鉛鐵則惡，惡不重禁之，不足以懲息。

translations.literal: When casting coin, if lead and iron are not mixed in there is no profit; if mixed in the coin is debased; unless debased coin is strictly forbidden, punishment and suppression will not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: If coin is cast without adulterating lead and iron, there is no profit in it; adulterate it and the coin turns debased. Unless debased coin is sternly prohibited, no penalty will check the abuse.

sentences.zh: 且方今塞其私鑄之路，人猶冒死以犯之，況啟其源而欲人之從令乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, at present we block the path of private minting, yet people still risk death to violate it — how much less can we open the source and expect people to obey the order?
translations.idiomatic: Even now, with the path of private minting closed, men still risk death to break the law — how then can we open the floodgates and expect obedience?

sentences.zh: 是設陷阱而誘之入，其不可三也。

translations.literal: This is setting a trap to lure them in — its third impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: That would be to set a trap and lure them in — the third reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 夫許人鑄錢，無利則人不鑄，有利則人去南畝者眾。

translations.literal: If private minting is permitted, when there is no profit people will not mint; when there is profit, many will leave the southern furrows.
translations.idiomatic: Permit private minting and, where there is no profit, no one will cast; where there is profit, multitudes will abandon the southern furrows.

sentences.zh: 去南畝者眾，則草不墾，草不墾，又鄰於寒餒，其不可四也。

translations.literal: When many leave the furrows, the wild grass goes untilled; when untilled, famine and cold draw near — its fourth impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: When many leave the furrows, the land goes untilled; when land goes untilled, cold and hunger draw near — the fourth reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 夫人富溢則不可以賞勸，貧餒則不可以威禁。

translations.literal: When people overflow with wealth, rewards cannot encourage them; when destitute and starving, threats cannot restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: When men are flush with wealth, reward cannot move them; when they are destitute and starving, punishment cannot restrain them.

sentences.zh: 法令不行，人之不理，皆由貧富之不齊也。

translations.literal: When laws fail to take effect and people refuse to submit, it is all because wealth and poverty are not evenly distributed.
translations.idiomatic: When laws fail and men refuse to be governed, it is always because wealth and poverty are unequally divided.

sentences.zh: 若許其鑄錢，則貧者必不能為。

translations.literal: If private minting is permitted, the poor will certainly be unable to do it.
translations.idiomatic: If private minting were permitted, the poor would certainly be unable to cast coin at all.

sentences.zh: 臣恐貧者彌貧而服役于富室，富室乘之而益恣。

translations.literal: I fear the poor would grow ever poorer while serving in wealthy households, and the wealthy would exploit this to grow ever more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the poor would grow poorer still, bound in service to wealthy houses, while the wealthy would exploit them and grow ever more unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文之時，吳濞，諸侯也，富埒天子；

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wen of Han, Liu Pi was a feudal lord, yet his wealth rivaled the Son of Heaven's;
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Wen of Han, Liu Pi was only a feudal lord, yet his wealth rivaled the Son of Heaven's;

sentences.zh: 鄧通，大夫也，財侔王者。

translations.literal: Deng Tong was a grandee, yet his wealth matched a king's.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tong was only a court grandee, yet his fortune matched a king's.

sentences.zh: 此皆鑄錢之所致也。

translations.literal: All this came of private coinage.
translations.idiomatic: All of this came of private minting.

sentences.zh: 必欲許其私鑄，是與人利權而舍其柄，其不可五也。

translations.literal: If you insist on permitting private minting, it is to hand others the profit and power while surrendering the handle — its fifth impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on permitting private minting, it is to hand others profit and power while surrendering the handle of state — the fifth reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 陛下必以錢重而傷本，工費而利寡，則臣願言其失，以效愚計。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty holds that coin is heavy and harms the capital stock, that labor costs are high and profit scant, then your servant wishes to speak of its defects, to offer a foolish plan.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty holds that heavy coin harms the capital stock and that labor costs exceed profit, then I wish to speak of its defects and offer my humble counsel.

sentences.zh: 夫錢重者，猶人日滋於前，而爐不加於舊。

translations.literal: When coin is heavy, it is as if people daily increase before one, yet the furnaces are not increased from before.
translations.idiomatic: When coin is heavy, demand for it grows daily, yet the number of furnaces does not increase.

sentences.zh: 又公錢重，與銅之價頗等，故盜鑄者破重錢以為輕錢。

translations.literal: Moreover, official coin is heavy and its value roughly equals that of copper; hence counterfeiters break heavy coin to make light coin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, official coin is heavy and its value roughly equals that of copper, so counterfeiters melt heavy coin to cast light coin.

sentences.zh: 錢輕，禁寬則行，禁嚴則止，止則棄矣，此錢之所以少也。

translations.literal: When coin is light, if prohibition is lax it circulates; if prohibition is strict it stops — when it stops it is abandoned; this is why coin is scarce.
translations.idiomatic: Light coin circulates when enforcement is lax and stops when enforcement is strict — and when it stops, it is abandoned; that is why coin grows scarce.

sentences.zh: 夫鑄錢用不贍者，在乎銅貴，銅貴，在採用者眾。

translations.literal: As for minting, when funds are insufficient, it lies in copper being expensive; copper is expensive because many use it in casting.
translations.idiomatic: Minting runs short because copper is dear, and copper is dear because so many draw upon it.

sentences.zh: 夫銅，以為兵則不如鐵，以為器則不如漆，禁之無害，陛下何不禁于人？

translations.literal: Copper — used for weapons it is inferior to iron; used for vessels it is inferior to lacquer — prohibiting it does no harm; why does Your Majesty not prohibit its use among the people?
translations.idiomatic: Copper makes poor weapons compared with iron and poor vessels compared with lacquer — prohibiting its private use would do no harm; why does Your Majesty not forbid it among the people?

sentences.zh: 禁於人，則銅無所用，銅益賤，則錢之用給矣。

translations.literal: If prohibited among the people, copper has no use; as copper grows cheaper, minting supplies suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Prohibit it among the people and copper finds no private use; as copper grows cheaper, minting supplies will suffice.

sentences.zh: 夫銅不布下，則盜鑄者無因而鑄，則公錢不破，人不犯死刑，錢又日增，末復利矣。

translations.literal: If copper is not distributed below, counterfeiters have no occasion to cast; then official coin is not broken, men do not incur the death penalty, coin daily increases, and agriculture again profits.
translations.idiomatic: Keep copper from circulating freely and counterfeiters lose occasion to cast; official coin will not be broken up, men will not face the death penalty, coin will increase daily, and agriculture will prosper again.

sentences.zh: 是一舉而四美兼也，惟陛下熟察之。

translations.literal: This is one move that joins four beauties; may Your Majesty examine it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: This is one measure that achieves four benefits at once — may Your Majesty weigh it carefully.

sentences.zh: 時公卿群官，皆建議以為不便。

translations.literal: At the time the high ministers and officials all memorialized that it would be inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the high ministers and officials all memorialized that the proposal would be impracticable.

sentences.zh: 事既不行，但敕郡縣嚴斷惡錢而已。

translations.literal: The matter was not carried out; only an edict ordered the commanderies and counties strictly to cut off debased coin, and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was not adopted; only an edict ordered commanderies and counties to ban debased coin strictly, and no more.

sentences.zh: 至天寶之初，兩京用錢稍好，米粟豐賤。

translations.literal: By the opening of the Tianbao era, coin in the two capitals was somewhat better, and grain and millet were abundant and cheap.
translations.idiomatic: By the opening of the Tianbao era, coinage in the two capitals had improved somewhat, and grain and millet were plentiful and cheap.

sentences.zh: 數載之後，漸又濫惡，府縣不許好者加價回博，好惡通用。

translations.literal: After several years it gradually grew debased again; prefectures and counties would not allow good coin to be bought back at a premium — good and bad circulated alike.
translations.idiomatic: After several years coin gradually debased again; prefectures and counties would not allow good coin to be bought back at a premium, and good and bad circulated alike.

sentences.zh: 富商奸人，漸收好錢，潛將往江淮之南，每錢貨得私鑄惡者五文，假託官錢，將入京私用。

translations.literal: Wealthy merchants and crafty men gradually hoarded good coin, secretly sending it south of the Jiang-Huai region; for each coin they obtained five pieces of privately cast debased coin, falsely claiming official coin, to bring into the capital for private use.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy merchants and unscrupulous men gradually hoarded good coin and secretly sent it south of the Jiang-Huai; for each coin they obtained five pieces of privately cast debased coin, passing them off as official coin to bring into the capital for private use.

sentences.zh: 京城錢日加碎惡，鵝眼、鐵錫、古文、綖環之類，每貫重不過三四斤。

translations.literal: Capital coin daily grew more chipped and debased — goose-eye, iron-tin, ancient script, ring-linked, and the like; each string weighed no more than three or four catties.
translations.idiomatic: Capital coin grew daily more chipped and debased — goose-eye pieces, iron-tin slugs, ancient-script counterfeits, linked rings, and the like; each string weighed no more than three or four catties.

sentences.zh: 十一載二月，下敕曰：「錢貨之用，所以通有無；

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year, an edict was issued: "The use of coin serves to circulate goods between those who have and those who lack;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianbao 11 (752), an edict declared: "The use of coin serves to exchange what one has for what one lacks;

sentences.zh: 輕重之權，所以禁逾越。

translations.literal: The balance of weight serves to forbid transgression.
translations.idiomatic: the balance of weight serves to forbid abuse.

sentences.zh: 故周立九府之法，漢備三官之制。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhou established the law of the nine treasuries, and Han perfected the system of the three offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou therefore established the nine-treasury system, and Han perfected the three-office mint.

sentences.zh: 永言適便，必在從宜。

translations.literal: Ever speaking of what is fitting and convenient, one must follow what is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: To speak always of what is fitting is to follow what circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 如聞京師行用之錢，頗多濫惡，所資懲革，絕其訛謬。

translations.literal: We hear that coin in circulation in the capital is largely debased; what is needed is correction and reform, cutting off error and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: We hear that coin in circulation in the capital is largely debased; what is needed is correction and reform to cut off error and abuse.

sentences.zh: 然安人在於存養，化俗期於變通，法若從寬，事堪持久。

translations.literal: Yet settling the people lies in nurturing them; transforming custom expects flexibility — if the law is lenient, the measure may endure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet settling the people requires nurturing them, and transforming custom requires flexibility — if the law is applied leniently, the measure may endure.

sentences.zh: 宜令所司即出錢三數十萬貫，分於兩市，百姓間應交易所用錢不堪久行用者，官為換取，仍限一月日內使盡。

translations.literal: The responsible offices should at once disburse three hundred thousand or so strings of coin, dividing them between the two markets; coin among the people used in exchange that cannot long circulate should be taken by the state in exchange, with a limit of one month to complete the exchange.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices should at once disburse some three hundred thousand strings of coin, dividing them between the two markets; coin among the people unfit for long circulation should be exchanged by the state, with one month allowed to complete the exchange.

sentences.zh: 庶單貧無患，商旅必通。

translations.literal: Thus the solitary and poor will be without worry, and merchants and travelers will surely pass freely.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the poor will be spared hardship and merchants and travelers will pass freely.

sentences.zh: 其過限輒違犯者，一事已上，並作條件處分。

translations.literal: Those who after the deadline violate the order, for one offense or more, shall all be punished according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Those who after the deadline violate the order, for one offense or more, shall all be punished according to statute.

sentences.zh: 」是時京城百姓，久用惡錢，制下之後，頗相驚擾。

translations.literal: " At the time the people of the capital had long used debased coin; after the regulation was issued, there was considerable alarm and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict was issued, the people of the capital, who had long used debased coin, were greatly alarmed and disturbed.

sentences.zh: 時又令于龍興觀南街開場，出左藏庫內排鬥錢，許市人博換。

translations.literal: At the time an order was also given to open an exchange ground on the south street of Longxing Abbey, disbursing stacked coin from the Left Treasury and permitting townspeople to exchange.
translations.idiomatic: An order was also given to open an exchange ground on the south street of Longxing Abbey, disbursing stacked coin from the Left Treasury and permitting townspeople to exchange.

sentences.zh: 貧弱者又爭次不得。

translations.literal: The poor and weak again struggled for place and could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: The poor and weak again struggled for place and could not obtain coin.

sentences.zh: 俄又宣敕，除鐵錫、銅沙、穿穴、古文，余並許依舊行用，久之乃定。

translations.literal: Soon another edict was proclaimed: except iron-tin, copper-sand, drilled-hole, and ancient-script coin, the rest were all permitted to circulate as before; after a long time order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon another edict was proclaimed: except iron-tin, copper-sand, drilled-hole, and ancient-script coin, the rest were all permitted to circulate as before; after a long time order was restored.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年七月，詔曰：「錢貨之興，其來久矣，代有沿革，時為重輕。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Qianyuan, an edict stated: "The rise of coinage has a long history; each age has seen changes, and weight has varied with the times.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Qianyuan 1 (758), an edict declared: "Coinage has a long history; each age has seen changes, and weight has varied with the times.

sentences.zh: 周興九府，實啟流泉之利；

translations.literal: When Zhou arose, the nine treasuries truly opened the benefit of flowing springs;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou arose, the nine treasuries truly opened the benefit of circulating wealth;

sentences.zh: 漢造五銖，亦弘改鑄之法。

translations.literal: When Han cast the five zhu, it also expanded the law of recoinage.
translations.idiomatic: when Han cast the five-zhu coin, it also expanded the law of recoinage.

sentences.zh: 必令小大兼適，母子相權。

translations.literal: Large and small must both be suitable, mother and child mutually balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Large and small must both be suitable, and mother and child coins must balance one another.

sentences.zh: 事有益於公私，理宜循於通變。

translations.literal: When the matter benefits both public and private, principle should follow flexible adaptation.
translations.idiomatic: When a measure benefits both public and private interest, principle requires flexible adaptation.

sentences.zh: 但以干戈未息，帑藏猶虛，卜式獻助軍之誠，弘羊興富國之算，靜言立法，諒在便人。

translations.literal: But because warfare had not ceased and the treasury was still empty, Bu Shi offered sincerity in aiding the army, and Sang Hongyang raised calculations to enrich the state; speaking quietly of establishing law, surely the aim is to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: But because warfare had not ceased and the treasury was still empty, Bu Shi offered his wealth to aid the army and Sang Hongyang devised plans to enrich the state; in legislating quietly, the aim is surely to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞第五琦奏請改錢，以一當十，別為新鑄，不廢舊錢，冀實三官之資，用收十倍之利，所謂於人不擾，從古有經。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Di Wu Qi memorialized requesting a change of coin, one for ten, separately casting new coin without abolishing the old, hoping to fill the resources of the three offices and collect tenfold profit — what is called not troubling the people, a principle from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Di Wu Qi memorialized requesting recoinage at one for ten, casting new coin separately without abolishing the old, hoping to fill the resources of the three mints and collect tenfold profit — what is called not troubling the people, a principle from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 宜職于諸監別鑄一當十錢，文曰「乾元重寶」。

translations.literal: The various mints should separately cast ten-for-one coin, inscribed "Qianyuan zhongbao."
translations.idiomatic: The various mints should separately cast ten-for-one coin bearing the inscription "Qianyuan zhongbao."

sentences.zh: 其開元通寶者依舊行用。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan tongbao coin should continue to circulate as before.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan tongbao coin should continue to circulate as before.

sentences.zh: 所請采鑄捉搦處置，即條件聞奏。

translations.literal: As for the requested mining, casting, apprehension, and disposition, report according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: As for the requested mining, casting, apprehension, and disposition, report according to statute.

sentences.zh: 」二年三月，琦入為相，又請更鑄重輪乾元錢，一當五十，二十斤成貫。

translations.literal: " In the third month of the second year, Qi entered office as chancellor and again requested recoinage of heavy-rim Qianyuan coin, one for fifty, twenty catties making a string.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year, Qi entered office as chancellor and again requested recoinage of heavy-rim Qianyuan coin, one for fifty, twenty catties making a string.

sentences.zh: 詔可之。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 於是新錢與乾元、開元通寶錢三品並行。

translations.literal: Thereupon new coin circulated alongside Qianyuan and Kaiyuan tongbao coin — three denominations in all.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon new coin circulated alongside Qianyuan and Kaiyuan tongbao coin — three denominations in all.

sentences.zh: 尋而谷價騰貴，米鬥至七千，餓死者相枕于道。

translations.literal: Soon grain prices soared; a dou of rice reached seven thousand, and the starved dead lay pillow to pillow on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Soon grain prices soared; a peck of rice reached seven thousand cash, and the starved dead lay pillow to pillow on the roads.

sentences.zh: 乃抬舊開元錢以一當十，減乾元錢以一當三十。

translations.literal: Then old Kaiyuan coin was raised to one for ten, and Qianyuan coin was reduced to one for thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Then old Kaiyuan coin was raised to one for ten, and Qianyuan coin was reduced to one for thirty.

sentences.zh: 緣人厭錢價不定，人間抬加價錢為虛錢。

translations.literal: Because people resented the unsettled value of coin, the market raised nominal prices as fictitious coin.
translations.idiomatic: Because people resented the unsettled value of coin, the market raised nominal prices as fictitious coin.

sentences.zh: 長安城中，競為盜鑄，寺觀鐘及銅象，多壞為錢。

translations.literal: In Chang'an city, men competed in illicit casting; temple bells and bronze images were largely broken up for coin.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an, men competed in illicit casting; temple bells and bronze images were largely broken up for coin.

sentences.zh: 奸人豪族犯禁者不絕。

translations.literal: Crafty men and powerful clans who violated the prohibition were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty men and powerful clans who violated the prohibition were unceasing.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹鄭叔清擒捕之，少不容縱，數月間搒死者八百余人。

translations.literal: Jingzhao Intendant Zheng Shuqing apprehended them, sparing none; within several months more than eight hundred were beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao Intendant Zheng Shuqing apprehended them, sparing none; within several months more than eight hundred were beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 人益無聊矣。

translations.literal: The people grew ever more desperate.
translations.idiomatic: The people grew ever more desperate.

sentences.zh: 上元元年六月，詔曰：「因時立制，頃議新錢，且是從權，知非經久。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Shangyuan, an edict stated: "Institutions are established according to the times; the recent discussion of new coin was only a temporary measure, known not to be lasting.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Shangyuan 1 (760), an edict declared: "Institutions are established according to the times; the recent discussion of new coin was only a temporary measure, known not to be lasting.

sentences.zh: 如聞官爐之外，私鑄頗多，吞併小錢，逾濫成弊。

translations.literal: We hear that beyond the official furnaces private casting is quite extensive, swallowing small coin and debasing it beyond measure into abuse.
translations.idiomatic: We hear that beyond the official furnaces private casting is quite extensive, swallowing small coin and debasing it beyond measure into abuse.

sentences.zh: 抵罪雖眾，禁奸未絕。

translations.literal: Though those punished are many, prohibition of wrongdoing has not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Though those punished are many, prohibition of wrongdoing has not ceased.

sentences.zh: 況物價益起，人心不安。

translations.literal: Moreover prices rise ever higher and hearts are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover prices rise ever higher and hearts are unsettled.

sentences.zh: 事藉變通，期於折衷。

translations.literal: The matter requires flexible adaptation, with the aim of a balanced settlement.
translations.idiomatic: The matter requires flexible adaptation, with the aim of a balanced settlement.

sentences.zh: 其重棱五十價錢，宜減作三十文行用。

translations.literal: Heavy-rim fifty-value coin should be reduced to thirty cash in circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy-rim fifty-value coin should be reduced to thirty cash in circulation.

sentences.zh: 其開元舊時錢，宜一當十文行用。

translations.literal: Old Kaiyuan coin should circulate at one for ten cash.
translations.idiomatic: Old Kaiyuan coin should circulate at one for ten cash.

sentences.zh: 其乾元十當錢，宜依前行用。

translations.literal: Qianyuan ten-for-one coin should circulate as before.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan ten-for-one coin should circulate as before.

sentences.zh: 仍令京中及畿縣內依此處分，諸州待進止。

translations.literal: Let the capital and counties within the metropolitan region be disposed of accordingly; the various prefectures await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: Let the capital and counties within the metropolitan region be disposed of accordingly; the various prefectures await further orders.

sentences.zh: 」七月敕：「重棱五十價錢，先令畿內減至三十價行，其天下諸州，並宜准此。

translations.literal: " In the seventh month an edict stated: "Heavy-rim fifty-value coin, first ordered reduced within the metropolitan region to thirty-value circulation — all prefectures throughout the realm should follow this.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an edict declared: "Heavy-rim fifty-value coin, first ordered reduced within the metropolitan region to thirty-value circulation — all prefectures throughout the realm should follow this.

sentences.zh: 」寶應元年四月，改行乾元錢，一以當二，乾元重棱小錢，亦以一當二；

translations.literal: " In the fourth month of the first year of Baoying, Qianyuan coin was changed in circulation to one for two; small heavy-rim Qianyuan coin was also one for two;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Baoying 1 (762), Qianyuan coin was changed in circulation to one for two; small heavy-rim Qianyuan coin was also one for two;

sentences.zh: 重棱大錢，一以當三。

translations.literal: large heavy-rim coin, one for three.
translations.idiomatic: large heavy-rim coin, one for three.

sentences.zh: 尋又改行乾元大小錢，並以一當一。

translations.literal: Soon Qianyuan large and small coin were again changed in circulation, all one for one.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qianyuan large and small coin were again changed in circulation, all one for one.

sentences.zh: 其私鑄重棱大錢，不在行用之限。

translations.literal: Privately cast heavy-rim large coin was not within the limit of circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Privately cast heavy-rim large coin was not permitted in circulation.

sentences.zh: 大曆四年正月，關內道鑄錢等使、戶部侍郎第五琦上言，請於絳州汾陽、銅原兩監，增置五爐鑄錢，許之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Dali, Di Wu Qi, Commissioner of Minting and related matters for the Guannei Circuit and Vice Minister of Revenue, memorialized requesting that five furnaces be added at the Fenyang and Tongyuan mints in Jiang Prefecture to cast coin; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dali 4 (769), Di Wu Qi, Commissioner of Minting and related matters for the Guannei Circuit and Vice Minister of Revenue, memorialized requesting that five furnaces be added at the Fenyang and Tongyuan mints in Jiang Prefecture to cast coin; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 建中元年九月，戶部侍郎韓洄上言：「江淮錢監，歲共鑄錢四萬五千貫，輸于京師，度工用轉送之費，每貫計錢二千，是本倍利也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jianzhong, Vice Minister of Revenue Han Hui memorialized: "The Jiang-Huai mints together cast forty-five thousand strings of coin yearly, delivered to the capital; estimating labor, transport, and delivery costs, each string costs two thousand cash — the principal is doubled in profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Jianzhong 1 (780), Vice Minister of Revenue Han Hui memorialized: "The Jiang-Huai mints together cast forty-five thousand strings of coin yearly, delivered to the capital; estimating labor, transport, and delivery costs, each string costs two thousand cash — the principal is doubled in profit.

sentences.zh: 今商州有紅崖冶出銅益多，又有洛源監，久廢不理。

translations.literal: Now Shang Prefecture has the Hongya smeltery producing ever more copper, and there is also the Luoyuan Mint, long abandoned and unadministered.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shang Prefecture has the Hongya smeltery producing ever more copper, and there is also the Luoyuan Mint, long abandoned and unadministered.

sentences.zh: 請增工鑿山以取銅，興洛源錢監，置十爐鑄之，歲計出錢七萬二千貫，度工用轉送之費，貫計錢九百，則利浮本也。

translations.literal: We request added labor to mine the mountains for copper, revive the Luoyuan Mint, establish ten furnaces to cast coin, with yearly output estimated at seventy-two thousand strings; estimating labor, transport, and delivery costs, each string costs nine hundred cash — then profit exceeds principal.
translations.idiomatic: We request added labor to mine the mountains for copper, revive the Luoyuan Mint, establish ten furnaces to cast coin, with yearly output estimated at seventy-two thousand strings; estimating labor, transport, and delivery costs, each string costs nine hundred cash — then profit exceeds principal.

sentences.zh: 其江淮七監，請皆停罷。

translations.literal: The seven Jiang-Huai mints should all be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The seven Jiang-Huai mints should all be suspended.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年正月，張滂奏：「諸州府公私諸色鑄造銅器雜物等。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan, Zhang Bang memorialized: "In the various prefectures, public and private casting of copper vessels and miscellaneous goods of every sort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhenyuan 9 (793), Zhang Bang memorialized: "In the various prefectures, public and private casting of copper vessels and miscellaneous goods of every sort.

sentences.zh: 伏以國家錢少，損失多門。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that the state has little coin and loses it through many channels.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant observes that the state has little coin and loses it through many channels.

sentences.zh: 興販之徒，潛將銷鑄。

translations.literal: Those who trade for profit secretly melt coin down for casting.
translations.idiomatic: Those who trade for profit secretly melt coin down for casting.

sentences.zh: 錢一千為銅六斤，造寫器物，則斤直六百餘。

translations.literal: One thousand cash yields six catties of copper; cast into vessels, each catty is worth more than six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand cash yields six catties of copper; cast into vessels, each catty is worth more than six hundred.

sentences.zh: 有利既厚，銷鑄遂多，江淮之間，錢實減耗。

translations.literal: Since the profit is so great, melting and casting have become numerous; between the Jiang and Huai, coin has truly diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Since the profit is so great, melting and casting have become numerous; between the Jiang and Huai, coin has truly diminished.

sentences.zh: 伏請准從前敕文，除鑄鏡外，一切禁斷。

translations.literal: Your servant requests approval according to previous edicts: except for casting mirrors, all should be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant requests approval according to previous edicts: except for casting mirrors, all should be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 」元和三年五月，鹽鐵使李巽上言：「得湖南院申，郴州平陽，高亭兩縣界，有平陽冶及馬跡、曲木等古銅坑，約二百八十余井，差官檢覆，實有銅錫。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the third year of Yuanhe, Salt and Iron Commissioner Li Xun memorialized: "The Hunan Office reports that on the border of Pingyang and Gaoting counties in Chen Prefecture there are the Pingyang smeltery and ancient copper pits such as Maji and Qumu, about more than two hundred eighty wells; officials were sent to inspect and verify that copper and tin are present.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yuanhe 3 (808), Salt and Iron Commissioner Li Xun memorialized: "The Hunan Office reports that on the border of Pingyang and Gaoting counties in Chen Prefecture there are the Pingyang smeltery and ancient copper pits such as Maji and Qumu, about more than two hundred eighty wells; officials were sent to inspect and verify that copper and tin are present.

sentences.zh: 今請於郴州舊桂陽監置爐兩所，采銅鑄錢，每日約二十貫，計一年鑄成七千貫，有益於人。

translations.literal: We now request two furnaces established at the old Guiyang Mint in Chen Prefecture, mining copper to cast coin, about twenty strings daily, estimated at seven thousand strings cast in one year — beneficial to the people.
translations.idiomatic: We now request two furnaces established at the old Guiyang Mint in Chen Prefecture, mining copper to cast coin, about twenty strings daily, estimated at seven thousand strings cast in one year — beneficial to the people.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，詔曰：「泉貨之法，義在通流。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, an edict stated: "The law of currency exists to circulate wealth.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year, an edict declared: "The law of currency exists to circulate wealth.

sentences.zh: 若錢有所壅，貨當益賤。

translations.literal: If coin is hoarded, goods must grow cheaper.
translations.idiomatic: If coin is hoarded, goods must grow cheaper.

sentences.zh: 故藏錢者得乘人之急，居貨者必損己之資。

translations.literal: Therefore those who hoard coin can exploit others' urgency, and those who hold goods must lose their capital.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore those who hoard coin can exploit others' urgency, and those who hold goods must lose their capital.

sentences.zh: 今欲著錢令以出滯藏，加鼓鑄以資流布，使商旅知禁，農桑獲安，義切救時，情非欲利。

translations.literal: We now wish to enact a coin law to release stagnant hoards, increase minting to supply circulation, so merchants and travelers know the prohibition and farming and sericulture find peace — the principle urgently saves the times; the intent is not to seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: We now wish to enact a coin law to release stagnant hoards, increase minting to supply circulation, so merchants and travelers know the prohibition and farming and sericulture find peace — the principle urgently saves the times; the intent is not to seek profit.

sentences.zh: 若革之無漸，恐人或相驚。

translations.literal: If reform comes without gradual steps, we fear people may alarm one another.
translations.idiomatic: If reform comes without gradual steps, we fear people may alarm one another.

sentences.zh: 應天下商賈先蓄見錢者，委所在長吏，令收市貨物，官中不得輒有程限，逼迫商人，任其貨易，以求便得。

translations.literal: All merchants throughout the realm who have already hoarded cash should be entrusted to the local chief officials, who shall purchase goods in the market; the state must not impose deadlines, forcing merchants; let them trade freely, seeking convenience.
translations.idiomatic: All merchants throughout the realm who have already hoarded cash should be entrusted to the local chief officials, who shall purchase goods in the market; the state must not impose deadlines or force merchants; let them trade freely, seeking convenience.

sentences.zh: 計周歲之後，此法遍行，朕當別立新規，設蓄錢之禁。

translations.literal: After a full year, when this measure is fully applied, We shall separately establish new regulations and set a prohibition on hoarding coin.
translations.idiomatic: After a full year, when this measure is fully applied, We shall separately establish new regulations and set a prohibition on hoarding coin.

sentences.zh: 所以先有告示，許有方圓，意在他時行法不貸。

translations.literal: Therefore We first give notice, granting latitude in method, intending that when the law is applied later, no indulgence will be shown.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We first give notice, granting latitude in method, intending that when the law is applied later, no indulgence will be shown.

sentences.zh: 又天下有銀之山，必有銅礦。

translations.literal: Moreover, wherever there are mountains of silver under Heaven, there must be copper mines.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, wherever there are mountains of silver under Heaven, there must be copper mines.

sentences.zh: 銅者，可資於鼓鑄，銀者，無益于生人。

translations.literal: Copper can supply minting; silver has no benefit to the living.
translations.idiomatic: Copper can supply minting; silver has no benefit to the living.

sentences.zh: 權其重輕，使條專一。

translations.literal: Adjust the heavy and light, making each regulation uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Adjust weight and value so that each regulation stands alone and uniform.

sentences.zh: 其天下自五嶺以北，見采銀坑，並宜禁斷。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm north of the Five Ridges, wherever silver mines are being worked, all should be forbidden and shut down.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm north of the Five Ridges, every active silver mine should be forbidden and shut down.

sentences.zh: 恐所在坑戶，不免失業，各委本州府長吏勸課，令其采銅，助官中鑄作。

translations.literal: Lest the mine-households in each place unavoidably lose their livelihood, entrust each to the chief officials of the local prefecture and district to encourage and supervise, ordering them to mine copper to assist the government's minting.
translations.idiomatic: Lest local mine-households lose their livelihood, each prefecture and district should charge its chief officials to encourage and supervise them in mining copper for the government's mints.

sentences.zh: 仍委鹽鐵使條流聞奏。

translations.literal: Further entrust the Salt and Iron Commissioner to draw up regulations and report by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Salt and Iron Commissioner should further be charged to draft regulations and report by memorial.
Close of edict.

sentences.zh: 四年閏三月，京城時用錢每貫頭除二十文、陌內欠錢及有鉛錫錢等，准貞元九年三月二十六日敕：「陌內欠錢，法當禁斷，慮因捉搦，或亦生奸，使人易從，切於不擾。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month of the fourth year, for current coin used in the capital — the twenty-cash deduction per string of 1,000, short strings within the count, and lead-tin coin, and the like — in accordance with the edict of the twenty-sixth day of the third month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan: "Short strings within the count are legally forbidden; fearing that apprehension would breed further fraud, it is better to make compliance easy — essential to avoid disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month of the fourth year, regarding current coin in the capital — the twenty-cash deduction per string, short strings, and lead-tin coin — the court followed the edict of the twenty-sixth day of the third month of Zhenyuan 9 (793): "Short strings are legally forbidden; fearing that arrests would breed further fraud, it is better to make compliance easy and avoid disturbance."

sentences.zh: 自今已後，有因交關用欠陌錢者，宜但令本行頭及居停主人牙人等檢察送官。

translations.literal: From now on, where short strings are used in commercial transactions, only the local trade head, lodging host, broker, and the like should inspect and deliver offenders to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when short strings are used in trade, only the local trade head, lodging host, broker, and the like should inspect the matter and deliver offenders to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 如有容隱，兼許賣物領錢人糾告，其行頭、主、人、牙人，重加科罪。

translations.literal: If there is concealment, sellers who receive payment are also permitted to denounce offenders; the trade head, host, persons, and brokers shall face increased penalties.
translations.idiomatic: If there is concealment, sellers who receive payment may also denounce offenders; the trade head, host, persons involved, and brokers shall face heavier penalties.

sentences.zh: 府縣所由祗承人等，並不須干擾。

translations.literal: District and county runners and attendants need not interfere at all.
translations.idiomatic: District and county runners and attendants need not interfere at all.

sentences.zh: 若非因買賣自將錢于街衢行者，一切勿問。

translations.literal: Unless one carries coin through the streets without cause of trade, do not question such cases at all.
translations.idiomatic: Unless someone carries coin through the streets without cause of trade, such cases should not be questioned at all.

sentences.zh: 」其年六月，敕：「五嶺已北，所有銀坑，依前任百姓開採，禁見錢出嶺。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month of that year, an edict stated: "North of the Five Ridges, for all silver mines, let the common people continue opening and mining as before; prohibit current coin from being taken out of the region.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year, an edict declared: "North of the Five Ridges, all silver mines may continue to be worked by the common people as before; current coin is forbidden from being taken out of the region."
Close of edict.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，制：「公私交易，十貫錢已上，即須兼用匹段。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, a regulation stated: "For public and private transactions of ten strings of cash or more, bolts of silk must also be used.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year, a regulation declared: "For public and private transactions of ten strings of cash or more, bolts of silk must also be used."

sentences.zh: 委度支鹽鐵使及京兆尹即具作分數，條流聞奏。

translations.literal: Entrust the Director of Revenue, Salt and Iron Commissioner, and Jingzhao Intendant to promptly work out the ratios, draw up regulations, and report by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Revenue, Salt and Iron Commissioner, and Jingzhao Intendant should promptly work out the ratios, draft regulations, and report by memorial.

sentences.zh: 茶商等公私便換見錢，並須禁斷。

translations.literal: Tea merchants and others who privately exchange cash through official channels must all be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Tea merchants and others who privately exchange cash through official channels must all be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 」其年三月，河東節度使王鍔奏請于當管蔚州界加置爐鑄銅錢，廢管內錫錢。

translations.literal: " In the third month of that year, Wang E, Military Commissioner of Hedong, memorialized requesting additional furnaces at the border of Wei Prefecture under his jurisdiction to cast copper coin, abolishing tin coin within his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of that year, Wang E, Military Commissioner of Hedong, memorialized requesting additional furnaces on the border of Wei Prefecture under his jurisdiction to cast copper coin and abolish tin coin within his circuit.

sentences.zh: 許之，仍令加至五爐。

translations.literal: Approved; he was further ordered to increase to five furnaces.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved, and he was further ordered to increase the number to five furnaces.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，戶部王紹、度支盧坦、鹽鐵王播等奏：「伏以京都時用多重見錢，官中支計，近日殊少。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, Wang Shao of the Ministry of Revenue, Lu Tan of the Directorate of Revenue, Wang Bo of Salt and Iron, and others memorialized: "We submit that the capital's daily use relies heavily on current coin, yet the government's disbursements have lately been especially scant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year, Wang Shao of the Ministry of Revenue, Lu Tan of the Directorate of Revenue, Wang Bo of Salt and Iron, and others memorialized: "We submit that the capital relies heavily on current coin for daily use, yet the government's disbursements have lately been especially scant."

sentences.zh: 蓋緣比來不許商人便換，因茲家有滯藏，所以物價轉高，錢多不出。

translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Huichang 6 (846), an edict declared: "Because new coin from casting Buddhist images, bells, and chimes across the circuits is proceeding in order, old coin must be allowed to circulate."

sentences.zh: 絹帛價稍增。

translations.literal: Silk and cloth prices rose slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Silk and cloth prices rose slightly.

sentences.zh: 文武百僚俸料，宜起三月一日，並給見錢。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials' salaries should from the first day of the third month all be paid in current coin.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials' salaries should from the first day of the third month all be paid in current coin.

sentences.zh: 其一半先給虛估匹段，對估價支給。

translations.literal: Half should first be paid in overvalued bolts of silk, disbursed at assessed value.
translations.idiomatic: Half should first be paid in overvalued bolts of silk, disbursed at assessed value.

sentences.zh: 」敕：「比緣錢重幣輕，生人坐困，今加鼓鑄，必在流行。

translations.literal: " An edict stated: "Recently because coin is heavy and currency light, the people sit in distress; increased minting must circulate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Recently because coin is heavy and currency light, the people sit in distress; increased minting must circulate."

sentences.zh: 通變救時，莫切於此。

translations.literal: Adaptive reform to save the times — nothing more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Adaptive reform to save the times — nothing more urgent.

sentences.zh: 宜申先甲之令，以誡居貨之徒。

translations.literal: Prior hoarding prohibitions should be enforced to warn those who stockpile goods.
translations.idiomatic: Prior hoarding prohibitions should be enforced to warn those who stockpile goods.

sentences.zh: 京城及諸道，起今年十月以後，公私行用，並取新錢，其舊錢權停三數年。

translations.literal: In capital and circuits, from the tenth month of this year, public and private use shall take new coin only; old coin temporarily suspended for several years.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital and the circuits, from the tenth month of this year, public and private use shall take new coin only; old coin temporarily suspended for several years.

sentences.zh: 如有違犯，同用鉛錫惡錢例科斷，其舊錢並納官。

translations.literal: Violators punished as for lead-tin debased coin; old coin surrendered to state.
translations.idiomatic: Violators shall be punished as for lead-tin debased coin; old coin surrendered to the state.

sentences.zh: 」事竟不行。

translations.literal: " In the end the measure was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the measure was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 開元元年十一月，河中尹姜師度以安邑鹽池漸涸，師度開拓疏決水道，置為鹽屯，公私大收其利。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Kaiyuan, Jiang Shidu, Intendant of Hezhong, because the Anyi salt pans were gradually drying, opened and dredged water channels, established salt colonies — public and private interests reaped great profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kaiyuan 1 (713), Jiang Shidu, Intendant of Hezhong, because the Anyi salt pans were gradually drying, opened and dredged water channels and established salt colonies — public and private interests reaped great profit.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月五日，左拾遺劉彤上表曰：「臣聞漢孝武為政，廊馬三十萬，後宮數萬人，外討戎夷，內興宮室，殫費之甚，實百當今，而古費多而貨有餘，今用少而財不足，何也？

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eleventh month of that year, Left Reminder Liu Tong submitted a memorial: "Your subject has heard that when Emperor Wu of Han governed, there were three hundred thousand stable horses and tens of thousands in the inner palace; abroad he campaigned against the Rong and Yi, at home he raised palaces — expenditure was extreme, in truth a hundred times the present — yet in antiquity spending was great yet goods remained in surplus, while today use is less yet funds are insufficient. Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eleventh month of that year, Left Reminder Liu Tong submitted a memorial: "Your subject has heard that when Emperor Wu of Han governed, there were three hundred thousand stable horses and tens of thousands in the inner palace; abroad he campaigned against the Rong and Yi, at home he raised palaces — expenditure was extreme, in truth a hundred times the present — yet in antiquity spending was great yet goods remained in surplus, while today use is less yet funds are insufficient. Why is this?"

sentences.zh: 豈非古取山澤，而今取貧民哉。

translations.literal: Is it not that antiquity drew revenue from mountains and marshes, while today revenue is drawn from the poor?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that antiquity drew revenue from mountains and marshes, while today revenue is drawn from the poor?

sentences.zh: 取山澤，則公利厚而人歸於農；

translations.literal: When revenue is drawn from mountains and marshes, public profit is ample and people return to farming;
translations.idiomatic: When revenue is drawn from mountains and marshes, public profit is ample and people return to farming;

sentences.zh: 取貧民，則公利薄而人去其業。

translations.literal: when revenue is drawn from the poor, public profit is thin and people abandon their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: when revenue is drawn from the poor, public profit is thin and people abandon their occupations.

sentences.zh: 故先王作法也，山海有官，虞衡有職，輕重有術，禁發有時。

translations.literal: Therefore when the former kings made law, mountains and seas had officials, foresters and gamekeepers had posts, weight and measure had methods, and prohibition and exploitation had seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the former kings made law, mountains and seas had officials, foresters and gamekeepers had posts, weight and measure had methods, and prohibition and exploitation had seasons.

sentences.zh: 一則專農，二則饒國，濟人盛事也。

translations.literal: First, farming is specialized; second, the state is enriched — a great affair benefiting the people.
translations.idiomatic: First, farming is specialized; second, the state is enriched — a great affair benefiting the people.

sentences.zh: 臣實為今疑之。

translations.literal: Your subject truly finds this puzzling in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject truly finds this puzzling in the present age.

sentences.zh: 夫煮海為鹽，采山鑄錢，伐木為室。

translations.literal: Boiling sea water for salt, mining mountains to cast coin, felling trees for dwellings —
translations.idiomatic: Boiling sea water for salt, mining mountains to cast coin, felling trees for dwellings —

sentences.zh: 農餘之輩，寒而無衣，饑而無食，傭賃自資者，窮苦之流也。

translations.literal: those beyond farming, cold yet without clothes, hungry yet without food, who hire themselves out to sustain life — these are the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: those beyond farming, cold yet without clothes, hungry yet without food, who hire themselves out to sustain life — these are the destitute.

sentences.zh: 若能以山海厚利，資農之餘人，厚斂重徭，免窮苦之子，所謂損有餘而益不足，帝王之道，可不謂然乎？

translations.literal: If the rich profits of mountains and seas could support those beyond farming, while heavy levies and onerous corvée were lifted from the destitute — is this not what is meant by "reducing where there is surplus to increase where there is lack," the way of emperors and kings? Can it not be called so?
translations.idiomatic: If the rich profits of mountains and seas could support those beyond farming, while heavy levies and onerous corvée were lifted from the destitute — is this not what is meant by "reducing where there is surplus to increase where there is lack," the way of emperors and kings? Can it not be called so?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下詔鹽鐵木等官收興利，貿遷於人，則不及數年，府有餘儲矣。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that Your Majesty decree the salt, iron, timber, and other offices to collect and develop profit, trading it among the people — then within a few years the treasury would have surplus stores.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes that Your Majesty decree the salt, iron, timber, and other offices to collect and develop profit, trading it among the people — then within a few years the treasury would have surplus stores.

sentences.zh: 然後下寬貸之令，蠲窮獨之徭，可以惠群生，可以柔荒服。

translations.literal: Then issue orders of lenient relief, remit corvée for the destitute and alone — thus the masses may be benefited and distant lands may be softened.
translations.idiomatic: Then issue orders of lenient relief, remit corvée for the destitute and alone — thus the masses may be benefited and distant lands may be softened.

sentences.zh: 雖戎狄、猾夏，堯、湯水旱，無足虞也。

translations.literal: Even Rong and Di, hostile Xia, or the floods and droughts of Yao and Tang would be nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Even Rong and Di, hostile Xia, or the floods and droughts of Yao and Tang would be nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 奉天適變，惟在陛下行之。

translations.literal: To follow Heaven and adapt to change — all depends on Your Majesty putting this into practice.
translations.idiomatic: To follow Heaven and adapt to change — all depends on Your Majesty putting this into practice.

sentences.zh: 」上令宰臣議其可否，鹹以鹽鐵之利，甚益國用，遂令將作大匠姜師度、戶部侍郎強循俱攝御史中丞，與諸道按察使檢責海內鹽鐵之課。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered the chief ministers to discuss whether this was feasible; all held that the profits of salt and iron greatly benefited state revenue, and he thereupon ordered Master Builder Jiang Shidu and Vice Minister of Revenue Qiang Xun, both acting as Vice Censor-in-Chief, together with the circuit inspection commissioners to examine and assess salt-and-iron levies throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the chief ministers to discuss whether this was feasible; all held that the profits of salt and iron greatly benefited state revenue, and he thereupon ordered Master Builder Jiang Shidu and Vice Minister of Revenue Qiang Xun, both acting as Vice Censor-in-Chief, together with the circuit inspection commissioners to examine and assess salt-and-iron levies throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 「比令使人勾當，除此外更無別求。

translations.literal: " Recently orders were issued for envoys to manage affairs; apart from this there are no further demands.
translations.idiomatic: Recently orders were issued for envoys to manage affairs; apart from this there are no further demands.

sentences.zh: 在外不細委知，如聞稱有侵刻，宜令本州刺史上佐一人檢校，依令式收稅。

translations.literal: Details outside the capital are not fully known; if there are reports of overcharging, each prefecture's governor and one senior aide should be ordered to inspect and collect taxes according to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Details outside the capital are not fully known; if there are reports of overcharging, each prefecture's governor and one senior aide should be ordered to inspect and collect taxes according to regulations.

sentences.zh: 如有落帳欺沒，仍委按察使糾覺奏聞。

translations.literal: If there is unrecorded embezzlement, it is still entrusted to the circuit inspection commissioners to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: If there is unrecorded embezzlement, it is still entrusted to the circuit inspection commissioners to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 其姜師度除蒲州鹽池以外，自餘處更不須巡檢。

translations.literal: As for Jiang Shidu, apart from the Pu Prefecture salt ponds, no further patrol inspection is required elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: As for Jiang Shidu, apart from the Pu Prefecture salt ponds, no further patrol inspection is required elsewhere.

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan, Shi Mou memorialized: "In Ze, Lu, Zheng, and other prefectures there is mostly crude salt; request that it be prohibited.

translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.
